It could be "running far past 30fps," too

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Somehow, Cyberleek returned. Now that GTA 6 is out and in players' hands, you might not think there would be much left to leak, but the group or individual behind the vegetarian pseudonym is now in the process of releasing an Xbox build of the game. That build could, Cyberleek threatens, turn into a PC version of GTA 6 in a matter of days.

"CL holds the full November 2026 build of Grand Theft Auto VI, and it is going out by torrent," Cyberleek says in a November 19 post captured by our friends at PC Gamer. "Now."

It's a typically dramatic message from the leaker, but early looks at the build from members of the hacking community suggest that the release is legit. It's just missing the main .EXE file needed to make it all go.

That executable is being "held on a countdown," Cyberleek claims. "Honest terms, as always: it is an Xbox build this time, not a PC build. CL does not care. This community will have it emulated inside a week, running far past 30fps. CL told you not to preorder for a reason. This is one of the reasons."

"Emulated" might be the wrong word, as no robust Xbox Series X/S emulators yet exist. But with recent advances in AI coding, getting console games playable on PC is starting to look downright trivial. Once a console game's been dumped, there's been little to stop a recompilation-based PC version from following, as we've seen with Nintendo's The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake.

In technical terms, of course, GTA 6 is a substantial leap over the Ocarina of Time remake, and recompilation devs might have a harder time getting a game driven by a massive open world and ray traced lighting running on PC at a playable frame rate. Regardless, once a pirated build is out there, an unofficial PC port is likely just a matter of time.

Rumors suggest that Rockstar plans to release an official GTA 6 PC port early in 2027, but the company hasn't even officially announced that the port will happen yet. Former Rockstar technical director Obbe Vermeij reckons that it'd be in the company's benefit to release a PC port early given the rise of AI ports, and the studio's hand might be forced sooner rather than later.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

There's reason to be skeptical of Cyberleek's claims since this is, after all, the same hacker who used the previous leaks as a way to pump up a $250,000 cryptocurrency grift. And yes, the crypto scam continues – Cyberleek says it'll release the executable early if its token reaches a $15 million market cap.

Still, Cyberleek says it'll make good on the release of the Xbox executable on November 23, regardless of the outcome of the crypto scheme. If that doesn't lead to a PC port, "CL will work to get a PS5 build." A bold sense of dedication at a time when other GTA leakers are becoming well aware of Rockstar's willingness to track them to the ends of the earth.

Check out our GTA 6 review to find out why it's a must-play masterpiece, or dig into our full GTA 6 guide if you're already making your way in Leonida.

#4010. GTA 6's Mandy 'Is a Lot of Fun' Says Real-Life Actress as PS5 Players Are Smitten

I knew when I was reviewing GTA 6 that bunny boiler Mandy was going to take social media by storm, and it was quite fun watching the web react to Chapter 1’s ‘Pipeworks’ mission as the game launched overnight.

Now it’s being played by millions, actress Lexie Shoaibi has revealed she stars as the character, who not-so subtly throws herself at Jason during a very early story mission.

I actually think this is one example of the game’s slightly more mature writing. Wait, don’t roll your eyes – just hear me out, okay?

While this whole quest is played more for laughs, it’s there to establish the strength of Jason and Lucia’s relationship, as Jason shows no signs of being tempted by Mandy’s advances.

“She’s a lot of fun,” Shoaibi said, after confirming she did voice acting and motion capture for the character. At the time of writing, her post on Instagram has received over 90k likes.

But the response on social media would suggest gamers think she’s more than a “lot of fun”.

One post by Complex, featuring a few images and the caption ‘Mandy from GTA 6’, attracted 37 million views in just a few hours. Pertinently, it’s been bookmarked 54k times.

I don’t want to analyse this character too deeply, but I think it’s the moment I realised Rockstar has really pushed the boat out here.

The sheer variety of body types, and the detail invested into them, is unprecedented really. Mandy is just one of many similarly realistic NPCs in the game.

And while the character is almost certainly a psychopath, it’s been amusing to see her go viral overnight.

#4009. Guide: Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Walkthrough (Switch 2 Remake): Guide To The Main Quest, Side Quests & Collectables

Zelda: Ocarina of Time is a dense adventure with many secrets to find, and while the critical path is fairly linear, it's rarely straightforward - asking you to pick up select items and upgrades before you can start exploring its many dungeons.

That's why a Zelda: Ocarina of Time walkthrough comes in handy. Though the Switch 2 version follows the same beats as the N64 original, we'd estimate around 10% of the game's puzzles and locations have been changed or updated - just enough to throw off those very familiar with the 1998 version.

This page features both an abridged and thorough walkthrough covering the critical path, plus a repository of our other Zelda: Ocarina of Time guides, from optional side-quests to items and collectables.

On this page: Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Walkthrough (Switch 2 Remake): Guide To The Main Quest, Side Quests & Collectables

If you want brief directions and as few spoilers as possible in terms of item unlocks and progression, then use the following abridged walkthrough to take you through the game. If you want extra specifics - including useful optional extras as you go - then check the following section.

For a more detailed walkthrough of the critical path, this section can explain specific steps on how to progress. If you want even more detailed step-by-step guides to the game's many dungeons, then follow the links to dedicated pages on each.

Before you can visit the Great Deku Tree, you must find a Sword and Shield, otherwise Mido won’t let you through. You can find the Kokori Sword in the Forest Training Center to the southwest (crawl through the vent to get there, then find it in the chest above), and the Deku Shield from the shop in the northeast by collecting Rupees found scattered around the village.

Visit the Deku Tree, complete the Great Deku Tree dungeon, and get the Kokiri’s Emerald key item and an instruction to head to Hyrule Castle. Now leave Kokiri Forest to the west to receive an Ocarina in a cutscene before leaving to Hyrule Field.

Head directly north along the path until you reach the castle drawbridge. The area inside is the Hyrule Castle Market - there’s lots of optional activities here, including the chance to get your first Bottle from the Potion Shop - and when ready, proceed to Hyrule Castle, where after getting the Weird Egg from Maron, you must make your way through the grounds to meet Zelda.

You'll now have Zelda’s Letter and learnt Zelda’s Lullaby on the Ocarina. The critical path is to Death Mountain via Kakariko Village, though you should visit the Lost Woods first (for Saria's Song, which you'll need shortly) and ideally, an optional visit to Lon Lon Ranch (for a Bottle and the first step in how to get Epona).

When ready, go east from Hyrule Field’s drawbridge and up the steps to Kakariko Village.

After finding all Cucco locations for a Bottle and visiting the Graveyard for the Sun’s Song (both optional), show Zelda’s Letter to the guard at the north exit. He gives you an optional errand - returning to the Hyrule Castle Market for a "proper shield" (the Hylian Shield) and also to start the Happy Mask Shop quest.

Guide All Great Fairy Fountain Locations In Zelda: Ocarina Of Time

Powerful upgrades for a small fee? Fairy 'nough

The aim is to reach Goron City. Hug the rightmost wall: this will take you up and round the corner, then back on yourself up the cliff. The path will now split: take the left branch to Goron City.

Inside Goron City, head to the lowest level, where on the north side is a closed door. Play Zelda’s Lullaby here to open it. Inside is Darunia. Talk to him, then play Saria’s Song (which you can get from the Lost Woods). This will see you unlock the Goron’s Bracelet, allowing you to use Bomb Flowers.

Now leave Goron City the way you came (the top entrance), then go directly right to see a Bomb Flower near a fence. Now you have the Goron's Bracelet, throw it over and you’ll bomb the entrance to Dodongo Cavern, allowing you to enter.

Once you have completed the Dodongo Cavern dungeon and picked Bombs and the Goron’s Ruby (the Spiritual Stone of Fire), feel free to scale Death Mountain for a Great Fairy Fountain location (unlocking Din's Fire) before heading off to Zora Domain.

Zora River - which leads to Zora Domain - is just east of Kakariko Village and Death Mountain on Hyrule Field.

Reach the end - the way there is fairly linear - and access Zora Domain by playing Zelda's Lullaby at the waterfall.

Inside, you must find the whereabouts of Princess Ruto by getting the Silver Scale in a mini-game at the top of the waterfall, then by visiting Lake Hylia via the underwater shortcut for a Bottle with a letter inside. (Our dedicated Zora Domain walkthrough features more specific directions for all these, by the way!)

Speak to King Zora, Bottle up a fish found in Zora Domain, then give it to the giant fish in Zora Fountain to access Lord Jabu-Jabu's Belly dungeon.

Once the dungeon is complete and the Spiritual Stone of Water is in your possession, head to Hyrule Castle. After the cutscene, dive in the moat and collect the Ocarina of Time, where you’ll then learn the Song of Time.

Head to the Temple of Time which branches off from Hyrule Castle Market. Inside, stand in front of the inscription at the far end, and play the Song of Time. Now go into the next room and retrieve the Master Sword.

After the cutscene, you’ll become Adult Link, and are told to head to Kakariko Village. Do so, then head to the Graveyard. On the left row of graves is a tombstone with flowers in front; push the stone and head down the hole. Now follow Dampe through the maze and at the end, you’ll receive the Hookshot.

To leave, play the Song of Time on the blocks, to emerge in the Windmill. Use this opportunity to get the Heart Piece opposite, then speak to the man to learn the Song of Storms - you’ll need this later.

With the Hookshot in hand, you can explore more of Hyrule, but when ready, head to Forest Temple: it can be found at the end of the Lost Woods, and inside the dungeon, you'll unlock the Bow and be rewarded with the Forest Medallion story item.

Complete the Forest Temple dungeon to unlock a Sage. At this point onward, upon returning to the Temple of Time, you can time travel back into Young Link by putting the Master Sword the pedestal. Also, to help, Sheik will teach you The Prelude of Light, which allows you to teleport back to the Temple of Time - a pretty handy shortcut.

As Adult Link, make your way to Death Mountain (it’s worth going into the Shooting Gallery in Kakariko Village now you have the Bow, which rewards you the Big Quiver to hold 40 Rupees as you go), then head into Goron City.

On the next level down is a Goron rolling around, and your aim is to detonate a Bomb near him so he stops. Once successful, the Goron will reveal their name is Link, son of Darunia, and will explain the Goron's plight.

Exhaust the dialogue options to receive the Goron Tunic - a red garb which allows you to withstand high temperatures - and directions to the Fire Temple, which is by heading to Darunia’s room (located on the bottom level at the back) and then by pulling the statue to reveal a route to the Death Mountain Crater.

Once in, go over the drawbridge using the Hookshot to meet Sheik, who will teach you Bolero of Fire. Now head through the left doorway, drop down and follow the passage to reach the dungeon, unlocking the Megaton Hammer and the Fire Medallion along the way.

Before you leave, it's worth going south across the bridge from the exit to Goron City in the Death Mountain Crater and using your Megaton Hammer on the cave entrance to get the Magic Meter upgrade from the Great Fairy Fountain within.

Head to the Ice Cavern, which is located in Zora Domain (or specifically, in Zora Fountain where you encountered Lord Jabu-Jabu as a child). Doing so will see you unlock the Iron Boots; make sure you grab a Blue Fire before leaving, and return to Zora Domain and use the Blue Fire on King Zora to free him and receive a Zora Tunic, which allows you to breathe underwater for an unlimited amount of time.

With both the Iron Boots and Zora Tunic in hand, we have everything we need to take on the Water Temple. Play the Serenade of Water to be teleported there when ready. Completing this will see you receive the Longshot - a Hookshot upgrade - and the Water Medallion.

Before we move onto the next temple, on this island is a plaque in front of you which hints at a puzzle involving the morning sun. If you are reading this as soon as the Water Temple has wrapped, the sun should still be rising: aim for the halo with your Bow and fire an Arrow, which will see it transform into a Fire Arrow on the platform ahead.

(As an aside, provided you have completed the previous three Adult Link temples, and have unlocked Epona, you now have everything you need to take on the optional Biggoron Sword trading sequence quest.)

Guide Biggoron Sword Trading Sequence Quest In Zelda: Ocarina Of Time

When you’re ready, head to Kakariko Village as Adult Link. When you arrive, a cutscene plays showing the place on fire, Sheik appearing, and a spirit emerges from the well. You’re then taught the Nocturne of Shadow, allowing you to travel to the Shadow Temple - though there’s a place to visit you need to visit first - the Kakariko well.

As it's currently blocked off as an adult, you need to return as a child. If you haven’t already, learn Song of Storms from the Guru-Guru inside the windmill, then return to the windmill as Young Link and play Song of Storms back to him (now you have the Nocturne of Shadow, the return journey will be a lot quicker).

Doing so will cause the windmill to spin out of control and lower the water in the well. Drop down and complete the Bottom of the Well mini-dungeon to get the Lenses of Truth.

Guide How To Get The Lenses Of Truth In Zelda: Ocarina Of Time

If you haven’t already, you also need Din’s Fire. This is acquired by visiting the Great Fairy Fountain location at the top of Death Mountain. Now you have Din’s Fire and the Lenses of Truth, play Nocturne of Shadow, then use Din’s Fire in the centre of the torches to gain access to the Shadow Temple, where you’ll get the Hover Boots along the way, and another Medallion.

With that done, it’s time to head to Gerudo Valley. It’s found in the west of Hyrule Field, and you need either the Longshot or Epona to make it over the bridge at the start.

Complete the Gerudo Fortress stealth section - essentially let yourself get captured, then find the four carpenters so you can explore freely - then past the Mirage Desert trials (you need the Longshot and the Lenses of Truth) to reach the Evil Desert Colossus area and the Spirit Temple.

This unlocks two new items - the Silver Gauntlets and the Mirror Shield - and another Medallion.

There are two optional extras in this region - a Great Fairy Fountain in Evil Desert Colossus (Nayru's Love; Bomb the cracked wall on the north side) and within Gerudo’s Fortress, the Gerudo Training Grounds (a mini-dungeon which grants the Ice Arrow).

Assuming you have now awakened every Sage and received every Medallion, it’s now time to head to the Temple of Time and start the final stretch of the game.

A cutscene will play and you’ll receive the Light Arrow, and an instruction to head to Ganon’s Castle.

Approach the lava moat around the castle to form a bridge with the help of the Sages. Now enter.

The Inside Ganondorf's Castle dungeon within is composed of six routes from a central hub, each with a 'Barrier' you must destroy; though you can tackle them in broadly any order, go for the Shadow Barrier first to get the Golden Gauntlets, which is required before tackling certain other routes in the dungeon.

Once that - and a brief trip to the Great Fairy Fountain just outside the castle beyond the bridge for a useful defensive upgrade - it’s time to scale the tower, or to halt your progress so you can mop up any remaining side-quests and collectables (see the end of this guide for a list) before the finale.

The tower within Ganondorf’s Castle is essentially a short gauntlet of battles until you reach Ganon himself at the top, and from there, it’s a linear stretch until the end credits. Good luck!

Here is a list of side quests, items and collectables you can find.

#4008. New Official Fallout-Inspired Game Announced, And It's Unlike Anything We'd Ever Expected

"A Wasteland Full of Cats, a Fallout-inspired adventure!"

In and amongst all of the GTA 6 news that's been happening this week, Bethesda has made a very quiet announcement about a new Fallout-inspired game, and it's one of the most bizarre crossovers we've seen in a while!

Simply put, Xbox and Bethesda are teaming up with the developers behind games such as A Building Full of Cats to create a Wasteland-themed game where you'll seemingly have to locate cats throughout the Fallout universe.

In other words, this would appear to be a hidden object game.

We'll throw some footage of one of this developer's Xbox titles down below so you can get an idea of what to expect. Their games are also always very inexpensive, and they also have some fantastic reviews on the Xbox Store.

There's obviously lots of other Fallout stuff in the works right now, including two remasters based on Fallout 3 and Fallout: New Vegas, as well as the much-anticipated Fallout 5. This new "inspired" game clearly just serves as a bit of fun to plug the gap, and we reckon it might actually do very well when it launches in the future.

It's cool to see Xbox partnering on lighthearted ideas like this! Long may it continue - do it with Halo and Gears next?

The GTA 6 mask neckwear lets you commit crimes with a bit more anonymity. As you might have noticed, cops are a lot more savvy in this new entry, pursuing you based on even your physical appearance. One way to hinder them identifying you is a mask.

The earliest mask you can buy is at Chuck's Tackle & Shot just down the road from Jason's house in Key Lento—if you're struggling to spot it, you can use the map index and navigate down to the Ammu-Nation tab. Any Ammu-Nation store should stock masks for purchase. In this case:

Buy and equip the mask and you're good to go. Jason will wear it on his neck by default but you can cover your face with it in the items menu. If you hold L1 then press R1 to cycle to items, move the stick over the mask, then press up on the D-pad to change the "Wear Style" to 1. Now you're ready for some crime.

#4005. Wolverine PS5's Sales Absolutely Plunged in October

Marvel’s Wolverine may have started strong in September’s Circana sales report, but it plunged in October.

Sony’s big PS5 exclusive for 2026, which attracted reasonable if utterly unremarkable reviews, ranked 14th in the latest US best-sellers list – dropping dramatically from first position the month of its release.

The game is now 15th overall for 2026 as a whole, down from 11th position in September. It’ll continue to fall with juggernauts like GTA 6 now officially out.

Couple other notes: Marvel's Wolverine dropped from 1st in Sept to 14th in Oct, ranks in top 15 YTD. On the YTD charts, less than $10M separates 8th place from 13th - it's a tight cluster.

The exclusive’s lore accurate lack of legs can likely be attributed to the game’s worse than expected reviews.

While it’s not universally disliked – we awarded it an 8/10, after all – fans understandably expect better from dev Insomniac.

Sony’s running discounts on the game during Black Friday to try and stimulate some enthusiasm around it, and I suspect this may be one of those titles that ends up in a lot of hardware bundles in the future.

To be fair, the platform holder seemed relatively satisfied with the title’s 2.4 million sales during its recent financial report.

I suppose it’s possible the launch numbers really did meet its expectations, but it may now be disappointed with the title’s long-term momentum – or lack thereof.

We’ll probably have to wait until its next investor update before we get more information.

There’s certainly some truth in that, and it’s always been the common wisdom. But I think the AAA market is a bit more complex now. Many of these big AAA games also get really long tail sales, they rely of that for making a lot of extra profit and getting people into the IP later.

Look at GoW: Ragnarok reportedly selling 20+ million units, yet only around 5 million were in the first week. Similar for Spider-man, Horizon, TLOU, GT7 and other big IP that keep selling long after release, they only hit those huge milestones from long tail sales. There was even an article on Bloodborne selling another 250k copies last year.

Of course not all sales are equal, financially day 1 sales will be at full price where as long tail sales will often be at a discount. And month 1 sales may also be used to judge a games success and make decisions for the studio going forward, they are still vital but don’t tell the whole story.

Then more and more people will find out about it, they will feel the hype, be unable to resist the temptation and buy it themselves.

It's why psvita failed. It wasn't embraced by the hardcore community that expected a sale, because the 3ds was struggling and had recently received one. #4004. HDR Expert Shares Their Three Recommended Display Settings For GTA 6

The good (and hilarious) folks over at HDTVTest have been looking at the HDR Calibration settings for GTA 6 on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, and they've discovered that the tool is actually slightly broken as things stand.

Some of the specifics go over my head a little bit to be honest, but in a nutshell, the figures that are displayed on the calibration tool don't fully translate into the game itself, leading to a potentially inoptimal picture.

As a result, they've published a new nine-minute video (which you can see up above) to explain the issues.

"The HDR calibration screen in GTA 6 can be misleading, because Rockstar's Max Brightness, Paper White and Black Levels settings interact in unexpected ways. To be clear, GTA VI's HDR rendering isn't broken… it's the calibration procedure that can give misleading results."

The video goes step-by-step on how they analysed the issues and tried to figure out the best possible HDR settings for GTA 6, and while their tests aren't fully concluded yet (there's another video to come in the future where they try multiple consumer displays), they've shared their initial best settings for displays capable of 1,000 nits or brighter.

Here are those three settings, but again, keep in mind that your TV must be capable of 1,000 nits of brightness or more, and that certain smart TV features or special HDR settings on your TV itself may interfere with the results.

If your display isn't capable of 1,000 nits, do a bit of Googling to try and find out the specifics for your TV/monitor, and then times that figure by two in-game. So, if you're working with a maximum of 600 nits, set the figure as 1,200.

I have to be honest and say I'm not seeing a lot of difference here, but I've also got an old TV with a max brightness of just over 600 nits, not to mention I'm using a few image-altering features that may be playing havoc with the settings. It's also noted in the video that this is generally based on playing in the dark, rather than in a brightly-lit room.

Have a play for yourself and see what you think - there's clearly a lot of people who are very thankful for these settings on YouTube and beyond, so we wanted to at least make you aware of them. The reality is that you may need to still do a bit of tweaking to find the perfect sweet spot for your setup though.

#4003. Sakurai Celebrates Kirby Air Riders' First Anniversary And Seemingly Ponders His Future As A Game Creator

He's apparently still working at "full throttle"

As we reflect on 25 years of Super Smash Bros. Melee, it seems game director Masahiro Sakurai is taking a moment to remind everyone that Kirby Air Riders has now been available for a year.

As highlighted by Sakurai on social media, the Switch 2 exclusive is officially one year old as of this week. It's received multiple updates since launch and Nintendo recently rolled out the last two amiibo.

In the game director's message, he also touches on his future as a game creator. Here's a rough translation of this part of Sakurai's post via EventHubs: "Time flies. I wonder how much more I'll be able to make".

Sakurai admittedly isn't getting any younger, and Kirby Air Riders included "everything" at launch, so it seems this is a genuine reflection on his future as a game creator. He has reportedly claimed to be semi-retired in the past, but this eventually led to Kirby Air Riders. He's also raised his future within the game industry on multiple other occasions.

Just earlier this week at the Famitsu 40th Anniversary Festival, Sakurai apparently revisited a column he had written about retirement, and how his decision depends on the demand for his work, and if he remains capable of delivering it (via OtakuKart). He's also questioned when his "spirit" might break. For now, though, he's still apparently working at "full throttle".

If we do hear any significant updates about Sakurai's future projects, or anything else he is up to, we'll be sure to let you know.

GameStop boss Ryan Cohen (last seen attempting to buy eBay) has called for the return of physical game discs, lamenting the lack of control players have over digital purchases in a chat with Bloomberg held on the eve of Grand Theft Auto 6's release.

In case you missed it, a media meteor impacted yesterday and blasted our landscape free of life. Grand Theft Auto 6 is here and—despite our Ted Litchfield's noble attempts to get you all thinking about Queen's Domain instead (you should play Queen's Domain)—it's all the world can talk about. It's also only available digitally.

"Unquestionably, the decision to move to all digital has hurt consumers, and it’s also hurt GameStop", said Cohen, remarking that players ought to be able to do with their purchased games as they will: "When you buy a game, you should be able to sell it, trade it or lend it to a friend". Cohen did not namecheck GTA 6 specifically, but did say that he had been speaking about this issue with all "the obvious" publishers.

GameStop, of course, makes a tidy chunk of change from resales of games traded in at its stores—a segment of its business that becomes impossible to maintain in a world without physical discs for players to bring in and sell. Publishers oppose trade-ins "because removing a used copy eliminates an alternative to buying new", says Cohen, accusing them of "taking away competition" by restricting sales to digital-only channels.

GTA 6 is a portent of the world to come. Earlier this year, Sony announced that PlayStation would drop physical discs starting in January 2028, and has held firm to that course in the face of a vocal player uproar.

Issues around game ownership have reached the point that politicians are weighing in: last month US lawmaker Richie Torres announced the Power To The Players Act, that would prompt the US Federal Trade Commission to protect players' access to purchased games, even in the case of online-only games that get unplugged.

"When you pay for a game, you should own it", said Torres. "Consumers must have the right to own, the right to play, and the right to transfer the games they buy. A game that can be taken away the moment a company pulls the plug is not a purchase. It is a rental disguised as a sale".

#4001. Talking Point: How Often Are You Willing To Play Games At 30FPS?

While GTA 6 has been receiving unbelievable praise and is technically considered one of the best video games of all time according to Metacritic, that certainly doesn't mean it's immune to criticism.

One of the big talking points both before and after launch has been that it's a 30FPS experience across all Xbox and PlayStation consoles, and if you're going from 60FPS back to 30FPS, there's definitely an adjustment period. Some people are absolutely fine with that, while others are finding it extremely difficult to go back.

For what it's worth, our friends at Digital Foundry have been analysing this in depth today:

Feature Why Isn't Grand Theft Auto 6 60fps?

Digital FoundryAnd could frame generation be the solution?

Rockstar Games has already confirmed recently that even the PS5 Pro doesn't come close to running GTA 6 at 60FPS due to the system's processor not being powerful enough, so we might be forced to wait until the next generation of consoles (and PC) before the game will become playable at 60 frames per-second.

"The PS5 Pro features an upgraded graphics processor and upscaling technology that we leverage to increase the game’s visual fidelity. While the PS5 Pro’s central processor is slightly better than the PS5 base console, it is not powerful enough to run the game’s complex simulation at higher frame rates.”

With all of this in mind, we're interested to hear what you think about playing games at 30FPS on Xbox, PlayStation or anywhere else. It's becoming much more common that 60FPS is the default these days, but there are still some phenomenal 30FPS-only experiences out there, and it's a shame to think people are missing out on them.

I personally much prefer playing at 60FPS if I can, and there are certain games I will avoid at 30FPS until they get a patch down the line (like Mafia: Definitive Edition), but when it comes to industry-defining masterpieces like Red Dead Redemption 2 and Grand Theft Auto VI, the last thing I'd want is for them to scale back the detail in order to squeeze in a 60FPS mode.

Being 30fps-tolerant would be an advantage for gaming, but we are not rare, I just asked Bing:

120–144 Hz → major improvement in smoothness and responsiveness

360–500 Hz → diminishing returns, but some users still perceive differences in latency and motion clarity

High-refresh displays (90–144Hz) make low framerates feel worse because the contrast is more obvious.

OLED screens reduce motion blur, making stutter more noticeable.

Poor frame pacing (uneven frame delivery) can feel worse than a stable 30fps.

Short answer: A large portion of the gaming community can detect and be bothered by framerates under 60fps.

The PS3/360 era is the era of the 'modern' TV technology.

I have a far bigger issue with uneven frame rate or uneven frame delivery than a stable, locked 30fps. 30fps isn't an issue unless you have uneven frame pacing. I'd rather have a consistent Frame rate than tearing and stutter/judder caused by frame rate drops - which VRR can help with nowadays but wasn't available on a TV until relatively recently.

But VRR, 4k 120hz etc are just the advancement of 'modern' TV's that replaced the CRT technology that ALL Domestic TV's were before they were replaced by Modern TV's. The very first Gaming Consoles and Home Computers were plugged into CRT TV's and 'Modern' TV's refer to the HD Flat Screen TV era and onwards that replaced the CRT TV's.

Your OLED uses the exact same 'Modern' technology and method of display as the HD TV's of the 360/PS3 era, the era of games like BioShock, Uncharted, Last of Us, Gears of War, Mass Effect etc etc - ALL Game of the Year winners and that also continued with the PS4/XB1 gen and games like the Witcher 3, Horizon Zero Dawn (PS4 and PS4 Pro) and God of War (PS4, PS4 Pro was 40-60fps in performance mode).

Point is, ALL games in the 'Modern TV' era that have been Game of the Year winners have predominantly been 30fps - RDR and RDR2, as well as GTA have always been (or targeted) 30fps (inc games like Assassins Creed, Dead Space etc). Its only when those 'old' games get brought forward to 'new' hardware that they target 60fps because the new Hardware isn't as CPU or GPU Limited as the Consoles they were built for. Bloodborne is another example of a 30fps game and award winning - built for hardware designed to use 'Modern' TV's like your OLED and won awards on Console connected to 'modern' TV's too

#4000. Guide: GTA 6: Radio Songs - All Music, Radio Stations, & Artists

As with the previous games in the series, GTA 6 has a staggering amount of both licensed and original music. There's so much to listen to, whether it's selected tracks during key story moments or you're just driving around with the radio on. In this GTA 6 guide, we're going to tell you everything you need to know about GTA 6's music.

On this page: All Radio Songs and Artists in GTA 6

Below is a list of every radio song in the game, divided by where and how they appear throughout GTA 6.

French electronic duo Justice has composed and produced the original score for GTA 6, providing music that soundtracks the entire experience. Here's the track list:

GTA 6: The Album is a selection of 34 original tracks produced just for GTA 6. Many of these also play on certain radio stations, listed below. Here's the album's track list:

As is tradition in the GTA series, GTA 6 features many radio stations you can listen to while going about your business in Leonida. Here, we list each station, along with all the songs they play. Songs that are totally new for the game are highlighted in bold.

As well as the radio stations, GTA 6 includes a number of original podcast series to enjoy. Each one features multiple episodes to listen to, unlocking as you progress. Here they all are:

The radio and podcasts can be listened to in a number of ways in GTA 6.

The most obvious way is while driving. In any vehicle, if the radio isn't on already, hold Left and turn it on with Cross/X. You can scroll through stations with L1 and R1:

To access podcasts, move the right stick down:

Outside of vehicles, you can find radios dotted around the environment; you can toggle them on with Left and choose a station (you cannot listen to podcasts on a radio):

Another option is to use headphones or earbuds.

Electronics stores sell over-ear headphones and earbuds, which allow you to listen to radio stations and podcasts while you're on foot.

To find an electronics store, open the map with Touch Pad, then use the directional buttons to reach Style, then Electronics. Nearby shops will populate the list, and you can set a waypoint from there:

Once you've bought a pair, equip them by holding L1, pressing R1 to access your items, then highlighting Headgear and pressing Cross/X as shown:

Now, you will be able to select radio stations and podcasts just like when you're driving.

GTA 6 features numerous musical artists and other celebrities, making cameo appearances in the game. Here they all are:

That's it for our guide to the radio songs in GTA 6. What are your favourite tunes to listen to in the game? Tell us in the comments section below, and be sure to check out our GTA 6 guide for much more.

#3999. Talking Point: What Are You Playing This Weekend? (21st November)

Pretty quiet week in the world of video games, eh? Nothing particularly groundbreaking released that we can think of...

Oh wait! Yes, that Grand Theft Auto 6 launched, didn't it? And it was a rather big deal. The game shot to the top of Metacritic's all-time best games list (tied with the original Ocarina of Time), and Digital Foundry weighed in on whether it'll ever come to Switch 2.

On a more Nintendo-related note, the Wii celebrated its 20th anniversary, Nintendo was named the most-nominated publisher at this year's The Game Awards, and a brand-new event got underway in Pokémon Pokopia.

All of this meant that it was a slightly quieter one in review land, but we still shared our thoughts on TANUKI: Pon's Summer (7/10).

Feature 20 Wii Exclusives You Should Track Down While You Still Can

Talking Point As A Parent, What Worries You Most About Gaming?

Nintendo's guide aims to highlight the benefits

So, is anyone playing something other than GTA this weekend?

I wrapped up Ocarina this week, and after a few days of feeling like an empty shell of a man (that ending still rips), I've been back to my backlog in an attempt to clear some before the year is up.

It's been Well Dweller that has been gobbling up most of my time. I think I'm about halfway through now, and it really is delightful. Hopefully I'll make a bit more progress with that this weekend, and maybe finally dip my toe into Pragmata too. Who has time for GTA, eh?

I’ve been absolutely barrelling through Ocarina with the kids, ticking off the Forest, Water, Spirit, and Fire Temples (in that order - a first for me!) in quick succession. A playthrough of the original over the summer definitely helped, so we’re one temple away from the big G, with about 70 Skulltulas bagged and five heart slots left to fill.

Beyond that, Queen’s Domain has me in its grasp, and I’ve also dipped into Well Dweller. Leonida is waiting to be explored on another console, too. Video games, huh? They’re per-ritty good. Have a good one, folks.

To many people’s surprise, I joined the GTA VI bandwagon late last night and was only able to play for an hour. So I’ll likely be following Vice City traffic laws like the previous games and be an upstanding citizen.

I’m also planning on getting some more OOT time in with my main save, getting collectables so I can finally start my “Mai-ster Mode” run. I have a pretty busy weekend regardless, so I hope I can get some gaming sessions in!

I am up to mission 65 in Earth Defense Force 5, and the game continues to throw new enemies (and weapons) my way! Finally, Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun 2 dropped on the eShop, but I must not neglect my The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time progress while serving the Emperor (surely no heresy here). I will also spend this Saturday at Lisboa Games Week, our annual video game celebration expo, and catch up with old friends while making new ones, playing fancy new and upcoming games.

My game of the week is Star Wars Rogue Squadron II: Rogue Leader. With the GameCube’s recent 25th American release anniversary, this incredible 2001 slice of Star Wars spaceship combat action turned a quarter of a century. I am still waiting for something that surpasses it. Time to chase those secret hidden upgrades and try to go for those gold medals again. Should be “fun” in my old age and diminishing reflexes. I will have to trust the Force on this one...

Those are our plans, but what about yours? Let us know what you'll be slapping in your Switch (2) in the poll below.

Jim came to Nintendo Life in 2022 and, despite his insistence that The Minish Cap is the best Zelda game and his unwavering love for the Star Wars prequels (yes, really), he has continued to write news and features on the site ever since.

I finished reading "The First Ghosts" by Irving Finkel. Fascinating topic, but I couldn't get on with the writing style, and it lacked focus. "After Dark" by John Lewis-Stempel is wonderful for nature lovers! Am now reading "The Penguin Book Of Demons".

ZOOT - I completed the forest temple, but have no desire to continue. ☹️ I will try to return to this.

Banjo Kazooie (Evercade) - Am still mainly playing during commutes. I now have around 80/100 Jigsaw Pieces, and 800/900 Musical Notes. Would love to 100% it. Gobi's Valley always messes me up! 😆

Have a lovely weekend, guys, and please take great care of yourselves out there.

Tonight I'm not seeing my friends so I'll just continue with my schedule:

I just finished playing Pipistrello and the Cursed Yoyo, which was great with fun puzzles and a good challenge.

That means I can finally start The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, which I received on release day but held off playing until I’d finished Pipistrello. I’ve played it a few times and expect it to be as excellent as always.

Still playing Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, Theodora’s path. Thinking on going back to Divinity: Original Sin 2 before I forget what’s going on. I’m in the middle of Act 2 and need to respec the whole group as battles are a nightmare with the current setup.

100% Ocarina last night, plus got all the Hall of Fallen Foes Zelda Notes medals that I am going to get.So now it is time to play something else... Not sure what though.

GTA VI all day long. I dropped everything for this game. Thankfully, I did not listen to the crew, who said that the coolest thing ever actually sucks. I had no reason to doubt Rockstar. They always deliver, and then some. The game is even better than I could have hoped for. Jason and Lucia are great characters. It is so nice to help them get closer and deepen their love. Finally I can enjoy a real, living open-world game again, ever since Red Dead Redemption 2.

Greetings fellow video game enthusiasts. I'm about to kick Ganondorf's door down and give him what for in Ocarina of Time. I have a fair amount of gold skulltullas and pieces of heart to find before that though. Happy gaming time everyone.

Well, another week of completely ignoring GTA VI while seemingly everyone I know has moved to Leonida. My friends have been sending me videos of themselves painting their bedrooms, furnishing their houses and texting their imaginary girlfriends, who apparently live in the same village. From what I’ve seen, the opening hours look considerably cosier than I expected. Nintendo should seriously consider suing Rockstar for shamelessly ripping off Animal Crossing.

Even my own brother attempted to get in on the action, proposing that he could “borrow” my PS5 if he bought GTA VI, promising to “return” it in a few weeks. A remarkably generous offer, I’m sure you’ll agree.

Meanwhile, back in Hyrule, I’ve been having a perfectly normal week. I found a lovely Fairy Bow and immediately began firing arrows aimlessly into paintings, solved what can only be described as a Rubik’s Cube made of green ghosts (mercifully without a timer this time), and sprinted through corridors resembling a particularly unpleasant acid trip while Navi shouted “TWISTY!” at me.

There was also the immensely satisfying moment of remembering how to dry out a rather damp room, and a light spot of sword tennis against the phantom of an old acquaintance. All in all, a productive week in the Forest Temple.

As for this weekend, I’m taking my daughter swimming for the very first time today, which I’m ridiculously excited about. Then, once we’re both suitably exhausted, I intend to venture into the Fire Temple and put that lovely complimentary red tunic to good use that a grumpy young goron insisted I take. Seems like the perfect way to warm up on a chilly autumn weekend.

Hope everyone has a wonderful weekend, whether you’re enjoying the animal crossing sim GTA6 or continuing to save Hyrule from certain doom.

Suddenly got really bored of Splatoon 3 after three years of nearly daily play, so I've had a lot more time for other games. Currently playing though Pikmin 4 (less said about the update the better), TANUKI, and Trials in the Sky - 1st Chapter. Hoping to finish the latter by the end of next week in order to hit the ground running with Xenoblade Chronicles 3 - Switch 2 Edition on the 3rd of December.

Oh, and F-Zero 99! That's still great for a few races a day.

Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter is back to being the main, and it really just gets better and better as the story develops. I love the strategic combat on hard mode. This game offers exceptionally dynamic JRPG battles, where each feels quite different not just from other battles but also across the course of the individual battle--often in response to mid-battle switch ups in my own tactics.

Interspersed are shorter sessions with Shadow of the Ninja Reborn. I've nearly cleared hard mode with Kaede (♥️) and plan to start with Hayate right after. I tried playing a bit of the NES original too, and it's neat to see the level design is so similar to the remake!

I was underwhelmed by OOT Remake. It was much shorter than I remembered! And way too easy. It redefined what was possible when it released on N64, but it no longer feels like the "greatest of all time." These days, I'd rate Majora, Twilight Princess, or Skyward Sword higher for a classic 3D Zelda.

I have been playing on my Steam Deck OLED this week! The games I have been playing include TMNT: Shredder's Revenge, No, I'm Not A Human, and Peak. All wildly different experiences! As always happy gaming everyone! Enjoy your weekend!

My wife surprised me with GTA VI, so of course that is what I’m playing, much like the rest of the world. Similar to RDR2, I’m slowly getting a grasp on the controls and life sim mechanics. It can be a grueling process, but it will eventually become second nature.

That being said, I’ve been absolutely blown away by this game. I had been curious for years as to how Rockstar would create an open world experience better than RDR2, and I can safely say that it has been an astonishing and mind-bending.

This is a game that will have people discussing their adventures for years to come. Speaking of, I will share one of my (early) experiences.

I was driving to some rundown RV park nestled away in the middle of nowhere. As I was making my approach I saw a bloodied deer sprawled out on the rocky terrain. Once I got much closer, I see a literal Sasquatch mutilating its body. I was stunned, but I quickly hopped out of my vehicle, got my rifle, and chased after him, but to no avail.

As I make my way back to my vehicle through this thicket of bushes, muddy waters, and even some alligators, I hear gunshots in the distance. I, of course, had to investigate, and find myself stumbling upon a beat down hotel. I notice there is a door wide open, and unexpectedly hear screams. All of a sudden, there is a guy crawling on his hands and knees out of the doorway, bleeding profusely. Another scream happens.

Right there, in the hotel room, was another guy getting mauled and eaten to death by a tiger. I begin panicking as it notices me, and I begin shooting the animal multiple times before it croaks over.

Once the situation becomes calm, I ransack the hotel room. There was a flare gun, drugs, and lots of cash. Out of nowhere comes three hillbillies attempting to rob me. I quickly pull out my flare gun (on accident) and unload my ammo on these punks. They catch fire and succumb to their horrific injuries. The coast is now clear and I book it out of there.

This whole (chance) encounter was so unexpected and organic. It’s these in-between moments that solidifies Rockstar as the masters of their craft. The amount of detail and interactivity is truly awe-inspiring. I can’t wait to see what other events transpire in my next 100-hours of play.

As you probably can already tell, I'm a BIG fan of the Metroid Prime franchise, I consider it one of the best series I've ever played & one of the many very defining Nintendo giants the brand has ever brought to my gaming life.

So, inevitably, I decided to finally jump into the most recent entry of the series with Beyond and I'm absolutely loving it so far, with it being an evolution in several aspects while also not completely neglecting the core gameplay mechanics previous entries introduced to the formula. I love the little details like the visor reflecting Samus' eyes when opening the system menu, the interactivity with the world being close to what Corruption introduced with its motion controls, the emotional but impactful soundtrack & also the great visuals, especially on our 7.9 inch LCD display (I ask myself how great the game will be looking like when Nintendo will release the Switch 2 OLED model!).

Of course I can see where the frustration is coming from when players first experienced Beyond comparing it to the original series, but I also appreciate Nintendo & Retro Studios for taking a different, more cinematic & modern approach to it and I do still have the highest hopes that they will one day release the still remaining two titles of the trilogy remastered on our current day machine.

So, this is what my weekend will be looking like and as I've already said, I'm absolutely loving it. Thank you Alex for your in-depth & benevolent review on YouTube, it is greatly appreciated!

#3998. GTA 6 Smashes Multiple Sales Records And Earns Xbox Series S Praise In First 24 Hours

Update: "Grand Theft Auto VI day one retail sales reached $3.79 billion"

Update [Fri 20th Nov 2026, 10:02pm]: GTA 6 publisher Take-Two is now reporting that day one sales reached $3.79 billion USD, while also selling 32.5 million units pre-release. The $3.79 billion figure is based on "company estimates".

"Rockstar Games, a label of Take-Two Interactive Software, Inc. (NASDAQ: TTWO), is proud to announce that Grand Theft Auto VI day one retail sales reached $3.79 billion, setting a new record for entertainment across any medium, and becoming the biggest entertainment launch in history."

"Achieving a near perfect score of 99 on Metacritic and resounding critical acclaim, Grand Theft Auto VI sold 32.5 million units pre-release, a new record across all platforms."

Original Story: Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 has reportedly smashed all sorts of records within 24 hours of launch, and it's off to a great start on Xbox Series consoles.

As shared by GTA 6 Countdown, GTA 6 has launched to a near-perfect 99 score on Metacritic (151 reviews), apparently sold 24.5m copies in under 24 hours, and seen 2 million Xbox players take a trip to New Zealand to play the game early.

Sensor Tower's sales tracker also estimates $2.36bn (£1.8bn) in revenue from GTA 6 sales, with the console split mostly in favour of PS5, at a 75% to 25% share over Xbox. Still, the data suggests Xbox still took a whopping $588m from 6.15m units sold.

GTA 6 dominated Twitch viewership too, with 50m hours watched and 3.3m viewers during its busiest hour, beating the livestreaming site's previous record (held by Hogwarts Legacy at 1.2m) by more than double.

Beyond all the big numbers we're chucking your way, we've also spotted a lot of praise for the Xbox Series S version of the game. Whilst Digital Foundry was hit-and-miss on the report, the general response online is majorly positive.

It's good news, then, to finally put to bed the lingering question of whether GTA 6 would run well enough on Xbox Series S consoles. Judging by IGN's comparison, it's not all that different of an experience to Sony's flagship PS5 Pro.

For Xbox Series S owners, it's genuinely the best console bargain out there, especially with FSR 4.1.

Strangely enough, FSR 4.1 still isn't available yet on the Xbox Series X, yet it's already getting very close to PS5 Pro-level performance. Once FSR 4.1 arrives, the Xbox Series X should be able to go toe-to-toe with the PS5 Pro, especially considering that the differences are already quite small today.

The standard PS5, on the other hand, is really starting to show its technical limitations: no VRR below 30 FPS, no Dolby Vision, and a weaker CPU. That makes a noticeable difference in action-heavy scenes and frame rates, since those situations put more strain on the processor.

It also lacks some RDNA 2 features, such as hardware Variable Rate Shading (VRS), relying instead on software-based alternatives.

The Xbox Series X, with its 120Hz VRR support and more powerful CPU, tends to deliver a more stable experience than the original PS5. It just goes to show that Phil Spencer was right: the Xbox Series consoles never needed a mid-gen refresh. They were already ahead of the curve in several key areas, and Rockstar seems to be proving that with GTA 6.

@HonestHick LGs and OLEDs are great, but every TV technology has pros and cons, there isn't a perfect one. E.g. OLED isn't as bright so may not be the best choice in brighter rooms. And for lower frame rates, like 30fps games, it often looks choppier on OLED because the screen is too responsive and you notice it more. OLED amplifies that lower frame rate, whereas LCDs slightly blurring between frames with "sample-and-hold" smooths the transitions. The thing that is bad at high frame rates, becomes a benefit at low frame rates.

Personally I found playing the Switch much less pleasant on my LG OLED, before it broke, and actually ended up playing most Switch games on another TV because of this. (They also looked better on a smaller screen)

But for faster frame rates the motion clarity is much better (on the high end LG models) as are deeper blacks.

@HonestHick As for refunds I probably have a very unpopular take on this. But I don't think we should just be able to get refunds by default if we simply don't like a video game. It's entertainment, and with entertainment you take a risk, sometimes you like it, sometimes you don't. If I go to the theatre, cinema or sporting event and I don't like it, if my team lost, I don't typically get a refund. If I buy a movie and don't like it I don't usually get a refund. Why should we for games?

The one exception for me is performance. If a game doesn't perform well, or makes us motion sick, or similar then yes there should be that option, but I don't think, just because you don't like a game, there should be an expectation of a refund.

Steam is slightly different as every PC runs differently and you may need 2 hours to see if a game works at all on your hardware. Consoles on the other hand everybody gets the same performance. But if a game is broken, or performs poorly on your hardware, e.g. CyberPunk on XBO/PS4, then it should be easier.

@AI-Generation it would have to trim down on a lot of aspects, so things like npc numbers, traffic, how they react and go about their business, density of the world. A lot of things that make the game wonderful are tied to the CPU which is similar across all of them.

I imagine that rockstar are pushing both CPU and GPU right to the metal in these machines with this game. The PRO uses PSSR and ray traced shadows due to the extra GPU headroom which allows it to keep a stable frame pacing. To hit 60, they have to halve the time taken to generate a new frame and maintain the detailed simulation aspects of it all. CPU wise it only has a tiny more available which would result in an unsteady frame rate that would plummet throughout play.

Rockstar have confirmed the series s is using FSR 4.1.2 over their own solution which is why its a lower resolution, as it hits the GPU load but allows them to keep a steady 33ms frame pacing, so they have to balance it all by cutting resolutions right down internally, but this allows them to keep many things that make the game wonderful. For the record, the fact it looks and plays how it does on the S is a stunning achievement and deserves all of its flowers.

As for PS5 and Series X, they dont use either QSSR or FSR as its likely that it would impact frame times/pacing to much, the upscalers dont come for free in terms of computation, and these GPU's have a limit.

They ultimately went for the best solution that allows it to run to the level it does, and holds both the best frame pacing and frames per second.

A fan-made recap of the entire Multiverse Saga has made its way online, and it's a pretty dang good one in case you don't have time to catch up before Avengers: Doomsday.

The video, which can be viewed below, takes all 15 of Disney Plus's suggested titles to watch in preparation for the upcoming film and turns them into a pretty snappy and concise 6-minute clip.

The titles include: X-Men, X2, Captain America: The First Avenger, The Avengers, Avengers: Infinity War, Avengers: Endgame, Loki (seasons 1 and 2), Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings, Spider-Man: No Way Home, Black Panther: Wakanda Forever, Captain America: Brave New World, Deadpool & Wolverine, Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness, Thunderbolts, and The Fantastic Four: First Steps.

The Multiverse Saga | Road To Avengers: Doomsday @MarvelStudios @Kevfeige @Marvel #AvengersDoomsday https://t.co/erbhbXLXL0November 18, 2026

Marvel's been pretty good lately about making sure that you don't need to watch earlier projects to understand brand-new ones. For example, Echo was easily the most standalone Marvel project, though it did lead into Daredevil: Born Again and Wilson Fisk's decision to successfully run for Mayor of New York City. In VisionQuest episode 1, Vision gives the audience a quick rundown of what happened to him in Avengers: Infinity War and WandaVision.

My personal recommendation? The only thing you really need to watch before Doomsday is Avengers: Endgame... and maybe Loki, so that you have a solid understanding of the TVA.

Avengers: Doomsday hits UK cinemas on December 16 and worldwide on December 18. For more, check out how to watch the Marvel movies in order.

#3996. 'It's Unbelievably Hard to Achieve': Cyberpunk 2077 Boss Pours Praise on 'Masterpiece' GTA 6

From Night City to Vice City, the boss of CDPR has nothing but nice things to say about GTA 6.

With the PS5 release of Cyberpunk 2077, the Polish studio established itself as an open world big boy, having previously released one of the greatest RPGs ever in The Witcher 3.

And so it’s only fitting for co-CEO Michal Nowakowski to pour praise on Rockstar’s latest release, now the highest rated game of all time.

“Rockstar Games created a masterpiece that I am planning to explore in the coming weeks and months. Massive congratulations to the whole team who worked on the game. It is unbelievably hard to achieve what you just did. Hats off to all of you.”

I personally believe it’s going to take years, if not decades, to surpass GTA 6.

The sheer density of the open world, from its dizzying array of art assets to the complexity of its sandbox simulation, is just in another universe to everything else.

Even if you’re not enjoying the game, it’s hard to argue against the standards being set here.

Of course, a high bar will raise the levels of absolutely everyone. I personally can’t wait to see what CDPR delivers with The Witcher 4 and its next Cyberpunk game.

Huang claims "he couldn’t motivate them simply with money".

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

It's been a strange couple of weeks for former Nvidia CEO, Jensen Huang. The once tech leader admitted to an affair, only for multiple affair allegations to surface, and he was then ousted from the company. Now, as he reportedly mounts a comeback, The New York Times has published a report detailing an alleged decades-long philosophy of getting more work out of employees "through humiliation".

Reportedly, Huang told employees that they had become so rich that "he couldn’t motivate them simply with money", so the "only way he could grind more work out of them was through humiliation".

This method has reportedly been Huang's modus operandi for some time, with more than a dozen current and former employees claiming: "He has long used humiliation as a tool, excoriating employees in front of their peers with insults, personal attacks and violent comments, while telling them it was good for them or for the business."

That humiliation allegedly took many forms. One employee reported that Huang "said he would rip both arms off a subordinate and beat the person over the head to death with them. And he told another employee he would rip off the top of their head and 'pee on your brain'."

Two years ago, in a conversation with Stripe's Patrick Collison, Jensen Huang said, "I'd rather torture you into greatness, because I believe in you", and this behaviour appears to be an extension of that philosophy.

Huang has apparently been called out for this behaviour. In the NYT report, Michael Winston, a former senior vice president of human resources, claims he threatened to sue Nvidia in 2005, after allegedly being fired for objecting to Huang's conduct. He says it is “the most verbally abusive, threatening and intimidating behavior” in his career and notes that Huang “thinks he can get away with anything.”

This lawsuit was apparently settled confidentially for more than $1 million, and was not previously public.

The PC Gamer Circuit Breaker newsletter breaks down the latest PC gaming tech, and finds you the best deals on the best products

Still, Huang has quite a few supporters at Nvidia too. Reportedly, someone took to the Nvidia internal suggestion box before Huang's ousting to ask Nvidia to consider keeping him after the affair scandal, and this was met with 1,600 comments, the majority of which agreed with the claim. One said: "If you believe in the mission, bring back THE boss."

After this, a public petition titled "Bring Back Jensen" managed to achieve over 200,000 signatures. Huang's role at Nvidia can't be overstated, being the CEO since its founding in 1993. The gaming company turned AI company is worth trillions of dollars, and that no doubt means something to at least some employees who wouldn't be there without it.

Still, I can't say I'd be very happy if my editor told me they'd rip my arms off and beat me to death with them, regardless of how much money they're paying me.

#3994. Feature: Don't Have Your Wii Set Up? Here Are 20 Wii Games You Can Play On Switch

Many people reading this will have a Wii in the house. Even if it's collecting dust in the cupboard after launching 20 years ago, there's over 100 million of the things out in the wild, so the chances are that you or your family have access to one somewhere.

However, on the off-chance you don't have a Wii to hand — or you sold it years ago to save three DVDs' worth of space — don't fret. While the system has a selection of exclusives you can't easily play elsewhere, many Wii games have come to Switch in HD remastered form over the years.

So if you're jonesing for some Wii waggle but would rather use the Nintendo console already plugged into the telly, take a look at some of the highlights below, in alphabetical order.

A Switch remaster of WayForward's remake of the NES original, A Boy and His Blob hasn’t changed since its release back in 2009, but it’s well worth checking out if you’re after a decent puzzle platformer. The visuals still look incredible after all these years, with spectacular animation to boot.

Some aspects feel a bit outdated by comparison to more modern alternatives, with the inability to map certain abilities being a key culprit. Nevertheless, it remains a fun, breezy experience, and one that the younger generation of gamers in particular will adore.

This Nintendo-published remake includes not just DS' Another Code: Two Memories, or Trace Memory in North America, but also the Wii sequel Another Code R, A Journey Into Lost Memories (which never came out in North America).

This is a fine reworking of a couple of point-and-click cult classics from now-defunct studio Cing (who also did the excellent Little King's Story), with a touching narrative, weighty themes, and light puzzling.

Please note that some external links on this page are affiliate links, which means if you click them and make a purchase we may receive a small percentage of the sale. Please read our FTC Disclosure for more information.

Available separately or bundled in the BIT.TRIP COLLECTION, this was the first entry in Commander Video's Runner series, and both Runner 2 and 3 are on Switch eShop if you want the trilogy.

The WiiWare original garnered a 10/10 on this very website back in 2010. Worth a look, then.

In the great platformer pantheon, we're not talking all-timers here, but these are slick, solid efforts with plenty of personality. Both de Blob and its sequel are on Switch in HD form, so if you're jonesing to see how devs approached 3D platformers in the late 2000s, get this inked in your diary.

Epic Mickey was a bold and very fine piece of work, although one where you could still make out the work-in-progress ideas that didn't quite come to fruition with the level of polish Nintendo fans might expect. It reimagined the squeaky-clean mascot and put him in a much darker world than we had come to expect, adding a touching narrative and putting a spotlight on his 'forgotten' predecessor, Oswald the Rabbit.

The Rebrushed remaster makes some tweaks and adds mouse (heh) controls. One for fans of vintage animation and anyone who likes to see creators take exciting chances with the most established of properties.

Soapbox 10 Years On, We Need More Brave, Worthwhile Experiments Like Epic Mickey

Donkey Kong Country Returns HD is a fine way to play the 2010 original, but it’s also lacking any real reason for fans to double-dip beyond waggle-free controls. It’s less of a remaster and more of a port, which would be all well and good if it wasn’t being sold at such a premium. Maybe wait for a sale.

There's plenty of fun to be had, but grab the superior Donkey Kong Country: Tropical Freeze instead - or at least first.

A 2023 Deluxe remaster of 2010's original Return to Dream Land, the HD Switch version threw in various tweaks, a couple of new copy abilities, an epilogue with Magalor, and an assortment of minigames mostly cherry-picked from past Kirby games.

Worth a look even if you've played the original to death, and the choice pick if you never had the pleasure.

Klonoa started out on PlayStation, of course, with Door to Phantomile back in 1997. Lunatea's Veil followed on PS2 in 2001, and Klonoa Phantasy Reverie Series bundles remasters of them both into a single Switch package.

So why this here at all!? yells the person at the back who's been grumbling ever since they saw the lead image on the article.

Well, although developer Monkey Craft tweaked some elements to push it closer to Namco's PS1 original in look and feel, the first remaster here uses Paon's Wii remake as its foundation. So if you played the Wii version in 2008, you'll be right at home.

The 2011 WiiWare release was a remake of the PC original, but fortunately La-Mulana found its way to Switch in 2020 (alongside its sequel).

Though brilliant, La-Mulana is definitely one of those games that will only appeal to a dedicated few. This is not something you can casually play every once in a while and expect a great experience; it demands much more of you through its peerless puzzle design.

If you do give it the time of day, however, it proves itself to be one of the most intricately crafted Metroidvanias ever made. La-Mulana gets a strong recommendation, but with the caveat that you should expect to be frustrated and stuck often. Don’t be scared off by the daunting difficulty, though; this is one for the ages.

A sneaky early addition here, as this remaster of Vanillaware's Wii (and Vita) game isn't out until 4th February 2027.

A gorgeous side-on action RPG, 2009's Muramasa: The Demon Blade was ahead of the wave of side-scrolling platformers that would arrive from indie studios over the next few years, and its eye-catching adventure through Japanese folklore is still a treat many years later.

Definitely one to look out for in the new year.

Soapbox Vanillaware's Most Underrated Game Is More Than Just A Pretty Picture

Probably cult developer Suda51's most well-known work, No More Heroes came to Switch in 2020 along with its sequel ahead of No More Heroes III's launch the following year.

Crammed with okatu-fuelled pop culture references (but hailing from nearly 20 years when those references weren't quite so tired), this was an adrenaline shot for Wii owners in 2007 looking for something a bit different after a year of genial waggle.

Wii scored not one, but two Touchdowns (and Switch has so far doubled that). Grasshopper returned with a punchy sequel in 2010, which once again helped put some personality on the Wii shelves alongside all the sanitised, motion-based sports and party fare.

Ironing out some of the wrinkles of the original and throwing plenty more irreverence and off-the-wall antics from the mind of Goichi Suda, No More Heroes 2: Desperate Struggle is still the peak of the trilogy for many.

It may have debuted on the PS2, but Ready at Dawn's Wii port felt like a minor miracle back in 2008. It's a great game that came to Wii, and you can play it on Switch, so here it is!

Okami HD is an utterly fantastic piece of software; a 40-hour adventure that emulates Zelda wonderfully, adds in plenty of memorable mechanics, features one of the most beautiful art styles in gaming, and is completely playable on the go, to boot.

It may be showing its age a bit visually and its combat is sometimes a little on the easy side, but Okami is an important, fun, and notable landmark in gaming history — and one of the easiest recommendations for your Switch library.

Stretching things a little here, both Pikmin and Pikmin 2: This Time It's Pikminable* were both GameCube games that got Wii-specific releases in the New Play Control series which added pointer controls and other minor tweaks.

Both games are available on Switch, though, so I'm including them. In fact, all four mainline Pikmin games are playable on Switch, something which irritates Metroid Prime fans no end.

*I enjoy the idea that this could turn up in somebody's AI summary. Ah, it's the little pleasures that get us through the day.

Perhaps the best thing about Sonic Colors Ultimate is the menu option to change the logo and UI from the American English 'Colors' to the British English 'Colours', mirroring the regional variants of the original 2010 Wii release. Great attention to detail, and an example of the care and respect that went into this solid remaster.*

*Don't forget, you have to have a little fun every day.

Regardless of which you think is better, these are two of the finest platformers ever made, both on Switch and looking better than ever.

Nursing the gyro pointers is a minor irritation the originals didn't suffer from, but if you somehow missed either of these on the Wii, you've now got no excuse.

Buy Super Mario Galaxy + Super Mario Galaxy 2

Bringing the Wii launch game back with a lick of HD 13 years later, Banana Blitz HD featured more refined controls — or more specifically let you control the mazes with the analogue stick — to help you enjoy this batch of 100 levels.

The wider game was still let down by weird leaderboard decisions and some lacklustre minigames, though. Hardly a return to the monkey-in-a-ball heyday of Super Monkey Ball 2, but not bad.

The Legend of Zelda: Skyward Sword HD introduced a raft of technical improvements and quality-of-life updates that revitalised the Wii game.

The alternate button control scheme totally worked if you still couldn't get on with the motion controls, the graphics got a sensitively handled HD overhaul, and a once-bothersome sidekick was streamlined into something altogether more useful. The best way to play.

World of Goo is a bona fide indie classic and 10/10 video game in its original incarnation. Its Wii pointer controls married perfectly with the gooey puzzling, and the social satire provided a subtle narrative framework that elevated the entire game.

The Switch version comes with joys and cons. Touchscreen is a brilliant addition in handheld mode, but you'll need to recentre the gyro pointer controls a lot. A lot.

If you've played it previously, the Switch incarnation might be worth a second go for its portability and on-the-go co-op, but if it's your first time in the World of Goo, it's absolutely a must-play. And then there's the sequel to consider. There's goo in them there hills.

The third iteration of Monolith Soft's classic following the Wii original and the New 3DS version in 2015, Xenoblade Chronicles: Definitive Edition presented an already excellent JRPG improved in nearly every way, short of a complete reimagining.

With the Nintendo Switch 2 Edition polishing this gem even further, it's hard to recommend the original release these days unless you're a purist wanting the exact experience everyone else got back in 2011. This is a great update, and a worthy game to finish on.

Buy Xenoblade Chronicles: Definitive Edition – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition

A pleasant little selection, no? Before heading off, let's address a handful of questions...

Yes, I know there are technically 22+ here. The Pikmins were borderline and bundled, though, and there are two Mario Galaxies in a single entry, a couple of other fuzzy collections, and Muramasa isn't even out yet. It all comes out in the wash.

Not impossible! Presumably it would be Switch 2-only (as with the GameCube library). It would be simple enough for Nintendo to produce NSO Wii Remotes and Nunchuk controllers, as they have for previous retro consoles.

There are potential flies in the ointment, though. For one thing, the precision of the infrared Wii pointer would either need to be emulated with gyro or reproduced (meaning you'd need some sort of sensor bar equivalent to function with the new controllers). Either or both are possibilities, but it does introduce another layer of complexity.

Then again, we're talking about a company that requires an expensive Virtual Boy facsimile to access that system's library on Switch, so (much) stranger things have happened.

As for the library itself, as we've seen above, several first-party Wii games have already received the HD treatment on Switch, so there may be less incentive on Nintendo's side to duplicate those on NSO. Likewise, Switch Sports and Switch Sports Resort update many of the games from the Wii originals, so it's not like you can't play Wii Sports-style tennis already.

But bolstered with a good selection of third-party titles, a Wii NSO library could be a winner.

Along with our list of Wii exclusives (or, in a couple of cases, games originally released on Wii that only appeared elsewhere years later), I'd do bad things for a 4K remaster of the beautiful Kirby's Epic Yarn.

It would be great to have access to other exclusives like New Super Mario Bros. Wii - not everyone's favourite 2D Mario, but an important one. Likewise, it's a shame to have Super Paper Mario and other entries from big Nintendo series (hello, Radiant Dawn) locked to a 20-year-old platform.

But that's me - what about you? Let us know below which of the games above you've enjoyed most, and any others you've enjoyed revisiting on Switch.

#3993. Talking Point: What Are You Playing This Weekend? (November 21-22)

Welcome back, PX'ers! You know the drill by now: it's time to talk with us about what you're playing this weekend.

I'm fully expecting the comments section to be flooded with GTA 6 this and GTA 6 that. Totally understandable behaviour. So, I'll keep this WAYP brief. Be sure to check out our Black Friday sales roundup later today and let us know what you pick up!

Alrighty then, let's get into it. Here's what we're playing on Xbox this weekend:

GTA 6, right? No surprise that's what I'm going to be playing. Fraser had a monumental blast with the game, and talking with him about it has given me the biggest case of FOMO going. Woof.

Other than the obvious, I've been playing a lot of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. Well, I say playing, more like learning songs on the in-game ocarina. I learned how to play Orbiter by Noah Kahan because I went to see the lad play the London O2 this week. I made a silly Instagram Reel of what it was like to learn the song, if you're interested. It was really fun.

I've also been thoroughly enjoying co-oping It Takes Two and SONIC PICO PARK with my beloved. So, we'll probably play some more of those.

And so, from one sleepy boy: have a bleddy jolly weekend, PX!

Yes, I've already finished GTA 6 as part of our Pure Xbox review, but you better believe I'm going through it again. The first playthrough was very rushed, so I'm intentionally taking my time and aiming for at least 100 hours before I reach the credits. There's so much more for me to discover, and I might make some different decisions too.

Beyond that, I've also just bought GTA 4's Complete Edition in the Steam sales for my ROG Xbox Ally X, as while I do enjoy the Xbox backwards compatibility version, it's desperate for a visual upgrade at this point. It doesn't make sense to me that they've never done it - surely it'll print money as soon as it happens!

Review GTA 6 (Xbox) - The Most Breathtaking Open-World Game Of All Time

This is going to dominate your life for months!

Talk with us about what you're playing this weekend down below!

Now if all the GTA 6 fans would kindly go play the game & stop spam asking the few folks streaming other games when they are playing GTA 6 I would be most grateful.

Hope you all (even GTA 6 fans 😉) have a great gaming weekend.

#3992. These 7 PS5 Games Launched on the Same Day as GTA 6 Like Mad Men

What’s the definition of insanity? It’s got to be launching your game on the exact same day as GTA 6, which is likely to be the biggest release in history.

I do remember hearing, in the PS3 days, that some smaller publishers would specifically launch alongside Call of Duty titles, because they argued they could benefit from the increased store foot traffic and pick up secondary sales.

I wonder if that’s true in the era of the PS Store, where most players are preloading in advance and probably not exploring too far beyond the titles promoted on the homepage.

Nevertheless, I think it takes a brave and stupid soul to go head-to-head with Rockstar like this, so I respect that.

And y’know what, I’m going to give every game that competed with the seminal open world its flowers on this very page:

The House of Tesla: Definitive Edition probably looks like the best pick, depending on your penchant for puzzlers.

We won’t be reviewing any of these games for obvious reasons, but to be brutally honest, I don’t think we would have even if GTA 6 hadn’t come out.

Nevertheless, it’s interesting to see so many titles release on the exact same day as the biggest game of all time. A few major live services got big updates too, like Disney Dreamlight Valley.

Did you buy any of the above, and why? Let me know below – I’m genuinely fascinated!
