"I think it would be really weird to do if I hadn't worked on the first one"

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Knights of the Old Republic is my favorite RPG of all time, and a key reason why my love of video games developed as deeply as it did. My hopes for Star Wars: Fate of the Old Republic, a spiritual successor to BioWare's classic, are sky-high, and expectations from the broader community are similarly intense. Director Casey Hudson isn't too worried about that pressure, though – after all, he and much of the team at Arcanaut Studios made the original KOTOR and the Mass Effect trilogy.

"I think it would be really weird to do if I hadn't worked on the first one," Hudson admits in an interview for The Fourth Curtain podcast. "It would feel really strange. But I think, for us, we've got folks on the team who worked on that game and have worked on all the Mass Effect games since and other BioWare stuff."

Hudson says that experience "helps," because the studio knows "why we did things the way we did. We're not trying to fill someone else's shoes, despite the expectations being really high."

We still know very little about Fate of the Old Republic, other than the fact that it's a spiritual successor to KOTOR. What kind of gameplay systems will it build on? I can't imagine KOTOR's creaky D&D 3.5-based mechanics are going to make a comeback. What kind of story will it tell? It's going to have to be something all-new, with the entire Star Wars universe having been rebooted since KOTOR was new.

"The thing that supersedes everything is our passion and excitement for doing something amazing," Hudson says. "That has to outshine everything else, because you can't really know how to answer pressure, and it's hard to even really understand what other people want to play. But if you're so excited about making something that people are going to love, you're just passionate about it being amazing, that leads you to where you want to go."

That's maybe an obvious answer, but I appreciate that it's the one Hudson is providing. No new game can possibly live up to my nostalgic memories of BioWare's Star Wars RPG, and what I really want is a new game created by a team of people who are excited about what they're making. If it can tap into my old love for KOTOR, that's just icing on the cake.

Star Wars: Fate of the Old Republic director Casey Hudson says there'll be "new announcements" about the KOTOR successor next year

His love for games was sparked somewhere between Metal Gear Solid 2 and Knights of the Old Republic, and these days you can usually find him splitting his entertainment time between retro gaming, the latest big action-adventure title, or a long haul in American Truck Simulator.

The platform says the new AI training policy is aimed solely at improving storefronts and tools, but not everyone is buying it.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Update: Etsy told the New York Times on Friday that it intends to revise the policy.

Online marketplace Etsy is facing backlash from users over a recent change to its policies that allow it and other companies to use content created by sellers to train AI models. In response, numerous vendors have closed their online shops, and are encouraging others to do the same. Etsy, however, says the new policy isn't meant to "replace your creativity," but simply to improve storefront operations.

The offending bit is found in part 5, section C of Etsy's terms of use, effective as of December 16:

That seems pretty straightforward—anything you put on your Etsy page can be fed into the AI theft machine like Steve Buscemi in a Cohen Brothers film—and as reported by Cartoon Brew, it led to significant pushback from some Etsy users, including numerous store closures.

You might have heard of Etsy's new terms and artists fleeing the platform. We're out, too.

A post shared by Aaron Millard (@aaronmillardillustration)

In the wake of that reaction, Etsy vice president of customer operations James Ossman posted a separate update saying it's not really like that at all, and that "we do not use your content to train AI models designed to copy your original work or replace your creativity."

"When we describe how we may use your content, we're enabling actions like translating your listing descriptions so buyers around the world can discover your items, or featuring your listing photos in Etsy marketing campaigns to showcase your creative work," Ossman wrote. "We also use your content to develop tools that make running your shop easier, like listing optimization tools or stats summaries that help you better understand your shop's performance. As always, your needs and feedback help guide how we build and improve these tools."

As for providing third-party access to that content, Ossman said that too is for "services and tools that can help you run your business," and promised that "when we partner with third parties, we do so thoughtfully to help protect your content and data."

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

That hasn't satisfied everyone. Ossman's commitment doesn't exist within the actual terms of service, which as seen above states only that Etsy and partners can "use Your Content to develop, train, test and improve artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies." Ossman also noted in his update that the terms "prohibit scraping Etsy or unauthorized use of content from Etsy to train AI models," but that (as far as I can tell) applies to Etsy users and unauthorized third-parties, not Etsy itself or those it licenses.

That's not to suggest that Etsy is being underhanded, merely that the binding legal language is imprecise. Others also complain that AI training should be opt-in rather than on by default—and worse, there's apparently no opt-out option available at all, so users who are opposed to having their work used for AI training for any reason are out of luck.

Ironically, the blowup over Etsy's embrace of AI training comes just weeks after it earned plaudits for banning AI-generated recipes and patterns, a move Ossman said was necessary to establish "trust" in the platform: "Sellers need clear guidance and confidence that their creativity and craftsmanship will be represented fairly; buyers need to understand what they’re buying and the human involvement behind it."

However this ultimately shakes out, the Etsy AI backlash is emblematic of a growing problem on both sides of the buy-sell divide: People want refuge from the creeping tendrils of the AI behemoth, and overtly or insidiously it's becoming increasingly difficult to find one. The more that happens, the more people are likely to react forcefully when platforms like Etsy start edging in the direction, regardless of any promises (or even carved-in-legal-stone commitments) of good intentions.

I've reached out to Etsy to ask if the new AI policy might be changed in response to the complaints and closures, and will update if I receive a reply.

#3988. Atlus Doesn't Want You to Wait Yet Another 10 Years for Persona 7

By the time Persona 6 comes out, it'll have been at least 10 years since the launch of Persona 5. That's a very long time between mainline instalments, and developer Atlus doesn't want you to have to repeat the process again.

Via a new company interview with creative producer Kazuhisa Wada, it's revealed the Persona team within Atlus is working on "various things" to make sure the wait between releases isn't so long. "Persona 6 is not the end," Wada said.

"We are working on various things to ensure that you don't have to wait as long for the next instalment as we have in the past," Wada continued. "And in order to make Persona an even bigger IP, we are constantly thinking about creative ideas and developments that will not disappoint your expectations. Please look forward to what's to come from Persona."

Rumour Persona 6 Release Is Way Closer Than Most People Think

Rumour Persona 6 Blowout Primed for The Game Awards

Wada does not comment on what those things it's been working on are, but clearly, the studio wants to bring its overall development times down.

While there have been spin-off games that continued the story established by Persona 5, such as Persona 5 Strikers and Persona 5 Tactica, we're still waiting on the next main entry, Persona 6, almost 10 years later. It doesn't have a release date yet, but there's a lot of hope it'll be out on PS5 next year.

On its release, Wada said the sixth game is "even better than before, and we're feeling a real sense of accomplishment as we work on it". Basically nothing other than the logo is known about Persona 6, so fans will be hoping rumours tying more details to The Game Awards next month are true.

Preorders of GTA 6 totalled approximately 32.5 million copies.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Some very rough napkin math led to estimates that Take-Two Interactive expected to make as much as $3.5 billion during the Grand Theft Auto 6 launch period. It actually made more than that on the GTA 6 launch day: Rockstar says the game pulled in $3.79 billion in "day one retail sales," making it "the biggest entertainment launch in history."

By way of comparison, Avengers: Endgame, ranked on Wikipedia as the highest grossing movie of all time, earned a little more than $2.9 billion over its entire theatrical run. GTA 6 crushed that by nearly $1 billion in a day.

"It is with immense gratitude that we enter a new chapter of Rockstar Games with the release of Grand Theft Auto 6," Rockstar Games president and co-founder Sam Houser said. "We are incredibly humbled by the response from players around the world and we couldn’t be more excited to share this moment with you."

Strauss Zelnick, CEO of publisher Take-Two Interactive, had previously said that preorder levels of Grand Theft Auto 6 were "unprecedented" but declined to reveal specifics. It turns out he wasn't kidding: Take-Two Interactive also revealed today that GTA 6 sold 32.5 million copies in pre-release, which it said is "a new record across all platforms."

Those numbers are absolutely staggering: There was never any question that GTA 6 was going to be huge, but those launch days sales—sales from one single day—surpass Take Two's net revenue guidance for the entire quarter by nearly $400 million at the high end.

Given that there's still well over a month remaining in the holiday season, I'd expect that figure to rise significantly: I'm not an industry analyst but more than $4 billion before the year is over suddenly seems just about conservative. Beyond that, I won't even hazard a guess, but consider this: Grand Theft Auto 5, which sold a little over 11 million copies on its launch day in 2013, has now surpassed 230 million copies sold in total. The sky, to paraphrase one of Tom Petty's other songs, really is the limit.

#3985. Katsuhiro Harada Reveals The Pokémon He Wanted To Add To Pokken Tournament

Famous Japanese game director and producer Katsuhiro Harada, known for the Bandai Namco series Tekken, has revealed a Pokémon he wanted to add to the Pokémon fighting game Pokken Tournament but it didn't make the cut.

Harada, who worked as a producer on both versions of the game, wanted the fighting / dark-type Pokémon 'Pangoro' from Generation VI. As for why he wanted to include it, Harada thought it had a "really cool" design and almost looked like it was wearing a traditional Japanese school uniform.

There were many discussions before finalising the roster, and a lot of it came down to the gameplay and systems in place, along with The Pokémon Company's own requests. Here's what Harada had to say about this (via EventHubs):

Harada: "We had thorough discussions before finalizing the roster. There were Pokémon that the development team wanted to include from a gameplay and systems perspective, and of course, The Pokémon Company also had its own requests for which Pokémon they wanted to see in the game."

After the release of Pokken Tournament DX for Switch, the final roster included the following Pokémon (this included some Switch-exclusive and DLC Pokémon).

As you can see, the final roster is an interesting mix. Harada, who is now the CEO and game director of SNK's VS Studio, added how he was just personally happy at the time to see the lineup include Pikachu and Gengar.

Joe Locke says he was totally unaware of the surprise post-credits scene at the end of VisionQuest... because it didn't come with his screeners.

"I didn't know Wanda was in it," Locke said on The View. "I watched the episodes a few months ago because they sent it to me. Ruiardh Mollica, who plays Tommy Maximoff in the show, also expressed on his personal Instagram story that he, too, was unaware of the post-credits scene. Either it was a last-minute decision, or Marvel decided to keep it a massive secret for a reason. Either way, the inclusion of the scene sent ticket pre-sales for Avengers: Doomsday sky-high, and made perfect sense for the 'family reunion' aspect of VisionQuest season 1, so it all worked out for the best.

The scene sees good ol' Victor von Doom appear to resurrect Wanda Maximoff from the dead after she brought the Darkhold castle down on her at the end of Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness. When she wakes up, however, her eyes glow a ghastly bright green... implying that she is now under Doom's control. Ruh-roh!

#3983. Feature: GTA 6 Made Me Want to Be a Good Guy (or Girl)

I’m playing a new GTA game but I’m actually abiding by the traffic rules.

I’m playing a new GTA game but I’m clicking L3 and R3 to focus and targeting non-vitals.

I’m playing a new GTA game but I’m actually opting to defuse the situation when an NPC gets mad at me.

The more I reflect on my time with GTA 6, the more I realise this is not the GTA I necessarily grew up with, even though the carnage is always there bubbling beneath the surface.

That’s because just like GTA Vice City and GTA San Andreas, I do have the option to go on a reckless murdering spree.

I could stock up on grenades and sticky bombs and create chaos on a highway.

I could go to a beach and mow down innocent bystanders in a scene so gruesome it’d make Jack Thompson pass out.

I think this is the most remarkable thing about GTA 6 – it’s made me play differently to past titles, even though nothing has actually changed.

So, why is this? Why am I choosing non-lethal as much as humanly possible, when the game allows me to go mental if I want to?

Firstly, Jason and Lucia certainly aren’t saints by any stretch, but they just don’t seem like the type to go on a killing spree.

This isn’t the first GTA game to have protagonists with a slightly softer personality – GTA 4’s Niko immediately springs to mind, as does GTA 5’s Franklin.

But I think with romance being one of this game’s central themes, you really get to know these characters intimately.

It’s about the quiet moments, rubbing your partner’s feet in front of the TV.

It’s relatable – and if it’s relatable, then I think the vast, vast, vast majority of us are kind and caring to others.

Of course, this is still a video game and I racked up kills in the hundreds by the end of the campaign, but I never felt like I was doing it on purpose.

I made mistakes – I sometimes knocked cyclists clean into the air. I wouldn’t do that in real-life. But I did try to avoid these moments as much as possible here.

One other wrinkle is that the realistic graphics mean the violence is pretty visceral. It’s fascinating to think how much criticism the PS2 trilogy got at the time, when it looks like a cartoon compared to this game.

I wouldn’t say the violence necessarily deterred me from being a cold-blooded killer, but I can see how it would affect others.

And also it’s a gameplay mechanic, right?

Behaving recklessly and showing no real care for other virtual life will alter your criminal profile, and change how the world reacts to you.

I ended up with a personality trait sitting somewhere between saint and sinner, but I think that’s probably normal as you’re still going to have to punch an NPC in the mouth from time-to-time.

I’m sure there’ll be people who see the GTA series as more of an arcade game than the life sim it’s become in GTA 6, and there’ll be many who don’t like this change.

For me, I’m fascinated by how Rockstar subtly convinced me to play a GTA game like it’s not a GTA game. And I didn’t even really notice it until recently.

That’s just one of the title’s many, many achievements – and one of the reasons why it’s now the highest rated game of all time.

I’ve spent an unhealthy amount of time just perusing the shops, sights and people. It feels sort of like being on holiday.

In fact, I guess that sums it up. I went in expecting this to be an open world sandbox whereby every selfish nihilistic desire can be experienced, and come out after every play session instead feeling like I’ve been on holiday.

It’s an odd thought, but the way the story has so far unfolded, and the freedom I have, though lending itself so well to violence I’ve found it more rewarding to come out with a smile of gratitude and appreciation.

#3982. Feature: 50 Of The Best Discounted Games From Xbox's Black Friday 2026 Sale

It's official, Xbox's Black Friday sales are live! This year's offering is absolutely massive, so we're back to rummage through them all and pick out a banger or two for you.

The annual sale lives up to the hype yet again, with over 2,000 deals to get through. There's so many. Too many, in fact. Plenty of big games are reduced by 90%, whilst others are at historic lows. Lots to be excited about!

It's a hefty job sifting through Xbox sales, we get it. So, instead of having you waste your precious gaming time doomscrolling through the Xbox Store, we've handpicked 50 deals from Xbox's Black Friday 2026 sale. These recommendations come complete with trailers, descriptions, Game Pass availability, and whether each title supports Xbox Play Anywhere!

Of course you can find all of these games, and then some, by going to the "Deals" section of the Microsoft Store app on your Xbox console.

The second game of the FINAL FANTASY VII remake trilogy. After escaping from the dystopian city of Midgar, Cloud and his friends set out on a journey across the planet. New adventures await in a vibrant and vast world – sprint across grassy plains on a chocobo and explore expansive environments.

The award-winning FINAL FANTASY VII REMAKE INTERGRADE* retells the original story up to the escape from Midgar, with breathtaking visuals, fast-paced gameplay, and additional story elements. This RPG delivers unforgettable characters, a powerful narrative, and a hybrid battle system that blends real-time action with strategic, command-based combat.

Dead Island 2 is a thrilling First-Person Action RPG, stylish, vibrant and flooded with zombie infection. Explore iconic, gore-drenched Los Angeles. Meet larger-than-life characters. Slay countless foes in exquisitely bloody detail. And evolve to become the ultimate Zombie Slayer.

The sci-fi survival horror classic Dead Space™ returns, completely rebuilt from the ground up to offer a deeper and more immersive experience. This remake brings jaw-dropping visual fidelity, suspenseful atmospheric audio, and improvements to gameplay while staying faithful to the original game’s thrilling vision.

Play through all 9 films of the saga in LEGO® Star Wars™: The Skywalker Saga Galactic Edition and enjoy playing as over 400 characters from the expanded universe.

Become the legendary part man, part machine, all cop hero and bring justice to the dangerous, crime-ridden streets of Old Detroit.

Make your mark. Become a Legend. Own The Show™. Step up and take control of how you leave your mark in the most immersive MLB® The Show™ yet.

The story of Cal Kestis continues in Star Wars Jedi: Survivor™, a third person galaxy-spanning action-adventure game from Respawn Entertainment, developed in collaboration with Lucasfilm Games. This narratively-driven, single player title picks up five years after the events of Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order™ and follows Cal’s increasingly desperate fight as the galaxy descends further into darkness. Pushed to the edges of the galaxy by the Empire, Cal will find himself surrounded by threats new and familiar. As one of the last surviving Jedi Knights, Cal is driven to make a stand during the galaxy’s darkest times - but how far is he willing to go to protect himself, his crew, and the legacy of the Jedi Order?

Hell is Us is a 3rd-person action-adventure game that combines intense melee combat with the thrill of exploration. Explore a semi-open world to find answers to your questions and face mysterious creatures all along your journey.

Marvel’s Midnight Suns is the ultimate crossover event combining the rich story, character relationships, customization and progression of an RPG with the tactical strategy and combat mechanics of a revolutionary new card-based tactics game. Set in the darker side of the Marvel Universe, you will forge unbreakable bonds with legendary Marvel Super Heroes and dangerous supernatural warriors in the fight against the world’s greatest threat yet…the demonic forces of Lilith and the elder god Chthon.

Craig is a Staff Writer and former Video Producer at Pure Xbox, where he covers the biggest games in the world of Xbox.

#3981. Poll: Which Mario & Luigi: Superstar Saga Box Art Is The Best?

Ahoy folks, and welcome to another edition of Box Art Brawl!

Looking back on last week, we checked out Dr. Mario & Puzzle League for the GBA to celebrate its recent addition to the NSO library. Neither design in this instance was particularly enthralling, and this is perhaps evident in the final result. Japan just about managed to claim a win with 51% of the vote, with North America / Europe making up the remaining 49%. Oof, so close!

We're sticking with the GBA this week to peruse the box art designs for Mario & Luigi: Superstar Saga. Released in 2003, this was the debut title in the spin-off RPG series, and arguably still its best. It was remade for the 3DS (and we did a Box Art Brawl for that one, too), but man, there's something about those GBA visuals that just make it, y'know?

North America and Europe share the same design for this one, so they'll be teaming up against Japan. Let's do this!

The western design for Superstar Saga is so good, Nintendo essentially did it again with the 3DS version. It's busy, but we love the way Cackletta sort of looms over everything in the background, while the bros themselves strike some pretty sweet action poses. A great composition, overall.

Japan went weird with this one. We've got a completely white background here, broken by the large logo and the bros. That's not quite all though. We do love those silhouettes showing how to use 'A' and 'B' for the protagonists, while the placement of Peach and Cackletta at the top is just so random, we can't help but giggle at it.

Thank you for voting! We'll see you next week for another edition of Box Art Brawl!

Review Mario & Luigi: Superstar Saga (Wii U eShop / GBA)

Nintendo Life’s resident horror fanatic, when he’s not knee-deep in Resident Evil and Silent Hill lore, Ollie likes to dive into a good horror book while nursing a lovely cup of tea. He also enjoys long walks and listens to everything from TOOL to Chuck Berry.

Choosing one you know the result will be completely lopsided isn't fun.

I like the close ones, because it's fun to read everyone's comments, there's usually some good insights people have for making their case.

I love the western artwork, although the Japanese one is a nice nod to the original Super Mario RPG design. A lot of old Square RPGs, like Final Fantasy and Chrono Trigger, had that minimalistic "characters and logo on a white background" look.

North America/Europe for me as it shows more character and the setting first and foremost - also prefer it aesthetically, not to mention that the colors and composition also give a better idea of how wacky Superstar Saga is!

NA/EUROPE. The Japanese one is just too sparse. Even the silhouettes of Mario and Luigi have question marks—they seem just as puzzled!

Japan all the way. It set the gag for the series’ box art.

I love the simplicity of the Japanese design but went for the other…

This is a no brainer. I never really cared for the minimalistic approach of this series box art, so the western one is just so much better.

The japanese is very clean so obviously that one.

Less is more. Gaijin one is too cluttered.

I've always really liked this game's western box art. What's unfortunate is that I don't like the games as much as I used to.

I loved this game as a kid. I've attempted to replay it multiple times but it just doesn't grab me in the same way. I've never beaten any of the other games in the series despite playing the first 4.

I’m torn on this one. I do think the North America/Europe box art is better purely just based on showing more of the cast and a very tiny bit of the environment, but I actually prefer the minimalist look of the Japanese box art.

I've never cared for the minimalistic look on boxarts. So western one all the way. I just like artwork over single color backgrounds. Although that little doodle of Peach is cute

I just love their facial expressions on the Japan cover! Mario looks completely oblivious, and Luigi looks very confused. Gets my vote!

Is water wet? Does a bear ***** in the woods? Is the europe box art better?

This is the very first Mario game I played, and it's because of that Box Art. I remember distinctly seeing it at Toys R Us and wanting to pick it up. I knew Mario from Smash Bros & general awareness but really only played Pokemon and licensed movie kids games before that point. I bet not many can say their first true Mario experience was an RPG instead of a platformer.

This one wasn't really worth doing was it?

I do like the Japan box for what it is but it’s got nothing on the Western one.

The western cover shows Fawful, that alone makes it my choice. I like the Peach, Cackletta and Popple doddles on the Japanese cover, though. Also, I think I prefer the Japanese cover as the Cartridge Art, as shown below. I just wish that one also had the doodles.

Not wanting to get political, but this game makes me think the Mushroom and Beanbean Kingdoms might be like Mexico and the USA, respectively. There's a community of immigrant Toads in the Beanbean Kingdom, a Koopa Troopa in the Koopa Cruiser mentions a Beanbean immigration of Goombas, implying Bowser might be what in Mexico we call a "pollero" (a person that may illegally get people into the USA, but most likely he'll abandon them to their own luck).

There's also the fact Mario & Luigi have to cross the border legally (with Passports) and the unfavorable exchange rate of 100 Mushroom Kingdom Coins equaling 10 Beeanbean Coins. Coincidence or not, at the time of the game's release in 2003, it was almost the same exchange rate of the Mexican Peso to US Dollar at around 11.15 MXN per USD.

I'm convinced there's also a Beanald Trump that says "I hate those Toad immigrants!".

The American version was one of the last action box arts (other than PiT) after that all the games took the flat white background route.

This was the game I got with my GBA for my 13th birthday, in 2003, and was the reason I met my best friend in 2004, who is STILL my closest friend. This one is special to me

Any box art featuring Fawful is my automatic pick!

@HammerGalladeBro And they said Shakespeare was dead

I will admit I voted for Japan and I meant it. I just think the NA / Europe one is a little safe and typical. The Japan art is odd but it still conveys just enough about the game for me. Didn’t like it at first and then it grew on me about 30 seconds later.

I think it's interesting how from Bowser's Inside Story onwards, the North American/European box art mimicked the Japanese ones, with the more minimalist style. I've always preferred those, personally. The western ones are pretty cluttered.

But having said that, that style does seem slightly out of place for such a madcap series of games; the western cover here is much more what you'd expect and is a lovely piece of artwork, so I went with that one.

Although I'm not the biggest fan of Superstar Saga, there's something about the Japanese artwork which I find incredibly appealing. Maybe it's because it puts the style and personality of Mario and Luigi, which at the time was very unique to this game, front and centre. We're seeing these two iconic characters in a way we've never quite seen them before and that in and of itself is intriguing!

I don't recall seeing Luigi's socks anywhere else, so it has to be the gaijin one for moi.

Definitely the EU one for me. It has a lot more going on. I like the clean Japanese one, but the EU one would convince me to get the game.

I'm sorry, i just like the silhouettes lol

It's easier to make successful games when you hold onto the people who know how.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

If we're using Metacritic as a metric, Grand Theft Auto 6 is currently the best-reviewed game of all time. Between preorders and launch-day sales, it's already made over $3.7 billion in sales revenue. It's being lauded as a landmark achievement in game design, storytelling, and engineering. So how, exactly, did Rockstar pull it off?

Well, the billion-dollar production budget certainly helped. But a Bloomberg report offers an important insight into how GTA 6 was able to deliver on its promises: According to a spokesperson, 21% of Rockstar's staff—roughly 1,000 people—have been employed by the company for over 10 years. For many of its development leads and directors, that figure is closer to 20 years, or higher.

By retaining its employees for so long, Rockstar is able to capitalize on the kind of shared, institutional knowledge and honed creative process that developers build through years of collaboration. We've seen that same kind of continuity at other studios who've delivered some of the last decade's biggest hits: FromSoft director Hidetaka Miyazaki has attributed its wins with Elden Ring and Armored Core 6 to its developers growing with the studio, while the breakout sales successes of Baldur's Gate 3 and Helldivers 2 were delivered by developers who'd spent years sharpening their craft at Larian and Arrowhead.

That lesson—that making successful games is easier when you keep the people who know how to make games around—isn't one that the games industry at large has been adhering to: In its latest game developer survey, GDC reported that 34% of its respondents had been laid off in the last two years. 20% of laid-off respondents said they'd been laid off twice or more in 24 months.

From Halo to Dragon Age, we've seen how beloved game franchises can suffer when their studios endure employment turmoil. After it laid off 1,600 Xbox workers in July, Microsoft's own employees said that myopic job cuts at major game companies were weakening the games industry as a whole by dismantling its ability to produce quality games.

It's a bell we've been ringing a lot around here.

Still, while Rockstar boasts a deep roster of veteran employees, those devs aren't confident that they won't be the next ones suffering from mass layoffs: We've seen plenty of successful launches lead to job cuts in recent years. As the company enjoys GTA 6's record-breaking launch, fears like those are why over 1,600 Rockstar employees in the UK are currently voting on unionization.

#3979. GTA 6 Sells a Record-Breaking 32.5 Million Copies

The biggest entertainment launch of all time

I think we all knew it was going to be big, but this big? Rockstar has announced that GTA 6 sold a staggering 32.5 million copies during its preload period, setting a “new record across all platforms”.

That number is likely higher by now, because the press release’s wording implies it’s not counting launch day sales into the above total, which are guaranteed to be plentiful. (It’s only going to keep rising through Thanksgiving and Christmas, too.)

Rockstar says the game generated a frankly mind-boggling $3.79 billion on day one, making it the biggest entertainment launch in history. Estimates claim it cost about $1 billion to make.

It’s also eager to point out that the title is now the highest-rated game of all-time as well, with its near-perfect 99 Metacritic score nudging the N64 version of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time aside.

“It is with immense gratitude that we enter a new chapter of Rockstar Games with the release of GTA 6. We are incredibly humbled by the response from players around the world and we couldn’t be more excited to share this moment with you.”

The dev didn’t specify how sales were split between systems, but the expectation is the PS5 version sold best, with some estimates pegging it at around 75% of the total.

Sony was the primary marketing partner of the game, and promoted the fact it “plays best on PS5” (even though testing shows it’s broadly identical to the Xbox Series X version on base hardware).

This is just the beginning for GTA 6, of course, with no word on Rockstar’s plans for the next iteration of GTA Online just yet. The game is also expected to launch on PC in 2027 as well.

If you’re one of the 32.5 million people playing, don’t forget to check out our GTA 6 guide for tons of information on the game.

#3978. Poll: So, What Do You Think Of GTA 6?

It's early days, but let us know your thoughts so far

We've been talking GTA 6 all week here at Pure Xbox, but now it's time for the community to take centre stage! We want to know what you think about the new Grand Theft Auto based on what you've played so far.

It's no secret that GTA 6 has been reviewing better than pretty much any game in existence since its release a few days ago. As things stand, it sits alongside the original Ocarina of Time as the best game ever made on Metacritic!

We helped contribute to that with our "Outstanding" 10/10 review score here at Pure Xbox:

Review GTA 6 (Xbox) - The Most Breathtaking Open-World Game Of All Time

This is going to dominate your life for months!

I have no doubt that it's a 10/10 in my mind, but is it the joint-best video game of all time? That's a much harder statement to make, and I think it's going to need months and years before we can really evaluate it in that regard.

It should also be pointed out that despite the reviewers heaping praise on it, and the Xbox and PlayStation store ratings being extremely high for GTA 6 right now, the game's user score on Metacritic is surprisingly low - so clearly there are plenty of people who aren't so hot on what they've played and/or seen so far.

We're well aware that many Pure Xbox users are probably just a few hours into their experience with GTA 6 so far though, and therefore it's very early days as things stand. We don't want you to give a definitive verdict on the game down below, but just let us know your initial thoughts and whether you're satisfied or not with your purchase.

Also tell us what you think of the vibe compared to GTA 4 and GTA 5 - we're very curious about that!

What did you pick in the poll above? Let us know in the comments section down below.

Fraser is the News Editor at Pure Xbox, where he spends his time reporting on the biggest stories in the world of Xbox and beyond.

@Sheppard As someone that plays a ton of Forza, I don’t have a hard time driving but the controls are touchy. The physics are surprisingly simcadey (in a good way), but the sensitivity is through the roof.

I’m not sure it’s my kinda game but it’s nothing if not competently made. The simulation element is really thorough, though I can’t say I feel like doing much of it. I can imagine someone really losing themselves in this.

Only played for 2hrs so far. I’ll let you know in a couple weeks

Game is an easy 10/10. Nothing can really compare to the world they have created and the story telling, voice acting is unmatched.

Last GTA games I put in quite a LOT of hours into was GTA3 and its spin offs but GTA4 put me off the Franchise and whilst I will say the game 'looks' impressive from a Graphical perspective, I've not seen anything that makes me want to buy it or would keep me playing, nothing that grabs me and makes me want to play it.

Its not the 30fps or the lack of a disc as I wouldn't buy if it was supplied on disc with a minimum 60fps option. Its not even the fact it doesn't hold that 30fps lock well either - I don't think its a game for me

I don't believe any game is truly worthy of a perfect 10/10 but GTA VI is definitely a 9/10 - 9.5/10 game. It's not without it's flaws like every single other game but it's a technical marvel that developers of open world games will be chasing for the next decade+.

A great high quality game but it's not a 10 that's for sure.

Edit: the game tries to get my attention via scripted moments throughout so it feels like I'm playing a role playing movie not a video game were I mentally put my attention into it so to be honest I can't stand games like this and it reminds me on how the AAA industry is all the same and it needs to change.

I was very disappointed, the hype put the bar so high that for me it just set unrealistic expectations, and I didn't feel it met the mark. But it's a good looking game, and the dialogues are great.

On a personal note, I don't like how the player character moves or aims, like you're underwater, kind of lethargic. It was the same with GTA V, which also put me off.

But I'm of the ilk who think GTA III is peak nostalgia, and San Andreas was the original and only masterpiece.

Decided to skip on GTA6 launch window for the Ocarina of Time. Can't really say if I made the better choice, but I know I'm happy with the choice I made

Either way, as they say we used to pray for times like these (having such awesome games launched in a span of week/s).

Solid 9 or 8 def not a damn perfect score

Feels like they took great things from GTA V and RDR2 and created this. Absolutely loving it. 10/10

@Sheppard depends said car. They all feel different. Jason’s car in chapter one is very hard to keep on the road.

Haven’t tried it personally yet, waiting until I can actually own it and play it above 30fps (which means either official pc release or recomp, whichever comes first). That said, one thing I don’t particularly care for is Jason’s voice. He sounds like he’s mumbling with a mouthful of food. Think they could have found better VO talent for his character.

It's good the world is very realistic but i have some nags the car driving is a little all over the place they've definitely brought back GTA4 style of driving. Roads are narrow as well in most areas and your first car has got a lot of power compared to the cars in every previous game you start with.

Swimming can be annoying but the worst is the fishing jesus Christ it should have been so much better and easier

It’s really a fantastic achievement in game design, but my wife and a friend of hers were watching me play and they were talking about how the game seems more like the Sims than GTA. Not in gameplay, but in tone, and I sorta agree. It’s very life sim in the 5-6 hours I’ve played so far. Everything seems top tier in terms of quality, but the game feels slow to start for me and I feel like I’m waiting for a big moment. It IS nice to see and play something that is so high quality across the board and universally played. It’s the only time this generation that it feels like something has brought the world together, which is nice too. I’d say second time because Elden Ring did that too, but the casuals are here for GTA in a way that they weren’t for Elden Ring.

I may get it when it gets a 60fps mode, either on PC or next gen consoles. Until then I’ll play around with it on my brother’s Xbox as he’s bought it.

Really early on in the game for me but I do have one pretty big gripe.

This might sound weird, but the result is a myriad of overly complex systems and gameplay that can be laboriously slow.

Walking or getting a taxi back to my car because a mission forced me to leave it on the other side of the map might be realistic but it is also boring and not respectful of my time.

But overall, too early to judge. Maybe the loop will click and i'll see what everyone else is seeing.

@somnambulance The start is definitely on the slow side! It really picks up in Chapter 2 though and will throw a load more traditional GTA type stuff at you but almost everything you’d expect from a GTA game has been revamped and made more interesting (IMO).

I'm about 12 hours in just slowly making my way through chapter 1 living my life and it's already the best game ever for me

@ozkrmz that's a very confusing message. You hard passed GTA 6 so assume it means you havent played it? but you found it boring because of working as a labourer? I'm not sure what parts have you working as a labourer? It's all very GTA for me in the hours I've played so far. Just a bit more expansive in variety on how to build up money (IE robberies, treasure hunting etc). And I'd say getting caught seems a lot easier to do at the moment so needs more thought, which after GTAV is a welcome change of direction.I keep reading negative comments about things I've yet to get to? Maybe it's further down the story 🤷‍♂️Regarding the frame rate complaints, my favourite games have all had terrible frame rates and never bothered me before, from OOT, Breath of the Wild , Elden Ring, Bloodborne and Skyrim. Makes me think theres a link to the best games and frame rates 🤔

@Medic_alert I get what you are saying. I remember that mission and getting the option to pay to speed up and choosing not to as not sure if it would be money well spent! To be fair I haven't had that again since as you can get you car taxied to you or you just steal a car to get you home so the game feels like you can choose to play it realistically or just simply not.

@Cikajovazmaj I went OOT first - great game and 2 weeks to finish it was perfect ahead of GTA6. Best 2/3 weeks of gaming I've had in years so far!!

I'm waiting for the PC release. I won't be double dipping.

@StonyKL I have just discovered the 'teleport' your car to you thing which helps. Albeit that was just one example.

It's just my view and an early one at that.

It feels very life-sim heavy in the early phases and I wasn't expecting that to such a degree.

Still making my way through Dragons Dogma 2 Dark Arisen, but can't wait to hit GTA VI next. Rockstar games are always several tiers above the second best devs in the world. Grading then on the same 10 point scale as other games is kind of insulting.

About 25 hours in and is a 10/10 to me. Mind-boggling technical achievement aside, it’s just a perfect encapsulation of where I live (Florida). I’d easily slot it next to my favorite games of all time-Persona 5, The Witcher 3, Mass Effect trilogy, Fallout 3, Oblivion, Bioshock…my favorite GTA title since San Andreas blew my mind 20 years sgo or so.

I hate review scores, but if I was forced to score GTA VI, it would be the easiest 10/10 I could give. Unbelievably good.

@GeeEssEff I’m hoping it picks up. I mean, it’s quite an accomplishment and I don’t want to sound like I don’t appreciate everything the game is doing because it’s incredible, but I’ll admit that 6-ish hours in, it’s felt a little busy work. I say that as someone that loved Fortune’s Weave, so I’m definitely not negative on having busy work. I just sort of feel like I’m still waiting for something, you know?

Played over 20 hours so far and still in chapter 1. Safe to say I'm enjoying it after a slow first hour.

10/10 33 hours in. There is no such thing as a perfect game, but there are masterpieces, and this is one of them. Much like a Zelda, Persona, Forza, Elden Ring, or BG3, it pushes its respective genre forward and creates a template for developers to push further and get better. GTA 6 will help CDPR build a better Cyberpunk 2077.

It runs well on the Series S, too, compared to the other consoles. I always appreciate the immersive worlds that R* create, and this one has gone to another level. It's a level of design, detail, and graphical fidelity that all AAA Western developers should aspire to in the coming years.

The record-breaking success is fully deserved.

@BAMozzy sounds like GTA should of stopped during the ps2 era as it’s gotten too realistic i guess

@oopsiezz i believe perfect games do exist . if people can make perfect shapes, arts and machinery, perfect coding, i dont think making a perfect game is far fetched but thats just me 😅

As is usually the case with GTA, jack of all trades but master of none.

It is what it is. No series has epitomised the term "bandwagoner" like GTA has. Even the most casual gamer will buy it and play it.

I'll tell you what though, it can't touch Alan Wake II (my pick for Game of the Generation) in the narrative and character development departments. Heck, very few games can. A true masterpiece.

@nomither6 I'd say they should have stopped before GTA4 because that's when they got too 'serious' more than too realistic. GTA4 wasn't realistic at all as its big city was really empty and the same few Shops, each with the exact same stock, was basically the only buildings you could enter.

I preferred Saints Row 2 to GTA although SR3 and SR4 went to far into being as much of a Schoolboy smutty joke but I still found these more 'fun'.

I think GTA3 and its spin offs were a bit more 'fun' and also benefitted from the transition to 3D which gave it something new and fresh at that time too. I also never enjoyed GTAO or RDRO.

As for perfect game, I don't think a Perfect game does exist and preferred the old method of rating games that would assess games on variety of different categories - graphics, performance, game-play, story, audio etc as that shows where games excel and/or could be better. No game ever releases that is way above average to score maximum points in every category to achieve a 'Perfect' score. I'm with others here that think a game that doesn't hold a locked frame rate can't be given a 'perfect' score BUT if it was broken down into categories, you can see where it perhaps isn't 'perfect'. In theory its perhaps possible to release a perfect game, but I think that someone will always feel like there are aspects that could have been better. A perfect Circle or Square for example cannot be more accurate, improved upon etc, but Performance isn't 'perfect' if it doesn't deliver a consistent frame rate with perfect frame pacing throughout.

I was out here whining about the 30fps, but I had forgotten how amazing R*’s games are. Been playing it and I’m just blown away. It’s been 8 years since RDR2, so I guess it’s just been so long I’d forgotten.

Either way, 10/10 so far. Having a blast and the details are just amazing.

#3977. Mailbox: Ocarina Intruders, Pikmin Day, Too Many Humans - Nintendo Life Letters

Hello, you. Yes, you. It's just us here today - everyone else is busy in Hyrule or Leonida right now.

In fact, it's been like that for most of the month, it seems, as the Nintendo Life Mailbox is looking pretty empty! So, it'll be a nice quick one this month. We'll have you back with your preferred ride — equine or automotive — in a jiffy.

Got something you want to get off your chest? Remember, we're ready and waiting to read about your game-related ponderings as we head into the holidays. Each month we’ll highlight a Star Letter, the writer of which will receive a month’s subscription to our ad-free Supporter scheme. Check out the submission guidelines at the bottom of this page.

So, let's slice open our correspondence...

I've been inspired to share in this letter about my first encounter with The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time following the feature you ran on this very topic, because it's a touching, unique story.

I was about 11 years old in 1998 and had been avidly following OoT in the magazines, absorbing every screenshot and article about this sword and shield weilding greened tuniced hero.

Bizarrely I'd never played a Zelda game before but something about it looked magical and exciting. So I did what any 11 year old would do. I asked for the game for Christmas.

So, Christmas morning arrives and I excitedly tumble down the stairs to the presents under the tree. I open them all but.... There's a pang of absence. No Zelda game. Where is it I exclaim!? And my mum sheepishly informs me that it didn't arrive in time for Christmas.

I cry. Real tears. I'm distraught. Inconsolable. For months I've waited for this amazing looking game and I can't play it.

What happened next is... I think... wonderful parenting.

While I was busy in my bedroom creating my own water temple with more tears than a kingdom (see what I did there?), my mum phones every parent of my school friends she knows until she finds someone with a copy of Zelda. And eventually, she does. She creeps up to knock on my door and says "Hey, Listen! I'll take you to your friends place, he has a copy"

And so, my tears stop and off I go to watch my pal play the game and suddenly a terrible Christmas becomes a brilliant one. The game is everything I imagine it to be and more and my mate and I spend hours solving Deku Tree puzzles and gasping at Hyrule Field's majesty.

So as we all enjoy the remake of Ocarina of Time decades later, I just have one thing to say: Thanks mum. You understood the stakes and you cared enough to help me get my Zelda fix that fateful Christmas of 1998.

And ever since that day, my life has been met with the least terrible of fates: I became a huge fan of Zelda and have bought every single one since on day one - no more painful Christmas mornings! YoshiTails

That is some above-and-beyond parenting, Mrs YoshiTails! We salute you.

I'm imagining what my mum would have said to some random mother ringing her on Christmas morning, asking if their kid could come over to play a video game. I assume she would have reacted in the classic British manner: agreeing to it with bemusement while silently seething, resenting the interloper for every surrendered mince pie.

I joke! I had no friends. I did have Zelda, though. - Ed.

Community "I Think Of Her Every Time I Play It" - Your Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Memories

We seem to have sleepwalked into an era of walking simulators.

I’m not talking about artsy indie games emphasising investigation over action, but big budget AAA titles starring main “characters” who look like they’ve walked out of a Hollywood movie. There are too many humans in games and it’s stifling the medium.

Back when the mascot character was king, protagonists felt properly differentiated both aesthetically and mechanically: Mario jumps, Sonic runs, Spyro flies, Crash bangs and wallops. Of these, only Mario could be called ‘human’, and even he has about as much in common with a real plumber as Sonic does with a real hedgehog.

Vibrant colours and exaggerated movements helped make the games legible on small screens when pixels, polygons and processing power came at a premium, and this gave games a unique vibe and feel. Now that we can better render humans in all their hairy, fleshy complexity, video game aesthetics have moved from ‘cartoonish’ to ‘cinematic’, and physics have followed suit.

Thing is, if I wanted to control a human, I’d put the controller down and go for a walk. (…Maybe not a bad idea actually). We’re meandering, clunky lumps of meat who navigate the world in a most pedestrian manner. Fine for a trip to the shops. Not the most inspiring thing to control in a video game.

It should be said that the ‘mascot character’ isn’t completely dead. The House of Mario was built by pixelated protags who carry the forward the flame of the 8-bit era. The portly purported plumber is still as satisfyingly springy as ever. DK has swapped pixels for vowels but continues to dish out delightful destruction like a primate possessed. Even the new squid-kids on the block - Splatoon’s Inklings - are unashamedly ‘gamey’, slipping slickly through their own mercurial fluids.

It’s a pleasant reminder that video games let us be anything we want: a bird (Untitled Goose Game), a plane (Star Fox) or even a kickflipping train (Denshattack). With that in mind, it seems a shame to be stuck as the same humdrum human that AAA titles insist on lumbering us with.

As film studios conglomerate and cinematic universes bleed into each other, I wish video games would embrace what makes them unique rather than dissolving into the same great multimedia melange. I’ve had enough of the homogeneous Homo sapiens-centric pseudo-cinema now synonymous with AAA game development and wish that more creative energies would be put into games that actually push the mechanical possibilities of the medium.

I disagree, purely because there are just so many games of all flavours out there. If you want to be a squirrel or a crab or an insect or anything else, there's never been a better time. Big, small, there's just so much incredible variety. If AAA isn't doing it for you, the other As have got you covered.

I get the sense perhaps you're reacting to the priority of animation over gamefeel in some cases - lumpy realistic animation versus snappy response? Pushing right on the stick and a moment later a soupy animation cycle transitions into the movement you've input (as opposed to Mario or Link responding instantly, if unrealistically).

If that's the case, I agree that Nintendo's approach is my preference, whatever form of animal, vegetable or mineral you're controlling. The animation of an Assassin's Creed or a GTA is incredibly impressive, but it's interminably slow if you're coming to it with a Mario mindset. I find I have to be invested in the cinema and 'show' of those games if they're going to click. My all-time favourites tend to have much more responsive controls, though. - Ed.

When Nintendo announced Pikmin Day this year for November 1st, it seemed to me that it was met with mixed reactions. People said that saying 11/1 looks like Pikmin is a bit of a stretch, and they didn't really announce anything particularly interesting. While this is true, I found it positively delightful, specifically the second half of the direct when Fuka Koshiba was revealed to be hired by Nintendo. While their conversation was a bit awkward (as Nintendo Direct dialogue always is), I thought it was super cool that they hired her just from seeing her posts on Instagram. And I've been loving the charming shorts that they've been releasing recently. And I'm not even a big Pikmin fan!

The direct was weird, certainly unnecessary, and a bit awkward, but that's what made it amazing. It was delightfully quirky, dumb, delightful, and wholly Nintendo.

I think any rational person will have responded to the 'Pikmin Day' declaration in the same way: wut. Anyone but Nintendo would have been torn to absolute shreds.

Frankly, though, with everything else going on in the world, if Shigsy wants to claim some random day for what might be their best series, crack on. A '1' looks like a Pikmin, you say, Miyamoto-san? Sure, fine. So, Pikmin 5 announcement next November, hmm? - Ed.

"For Pokémon day next year, I want a Pok" - Scottdevine53

That's all for this month! Thanks to everyone who wrote in, whether you were featured above or not.

Got something you'd like to get off your chest? A burning question you need answered? A correction you can't contain? Follow the instructions below, then, and we look forward to rifling through your missives.

Site News Love What We Do? Become A Nintendo Life Supporter!

Gavin first wrote for Nintendo Life in 2018 before joining the site full-time the following year, rising through the ranks to become Editor. He can currently be found squashed beneath a Switch backlog the size of Normandy.

In case anyone was wondering, I am also wishing for a Pok.

Here are my comments about the main letters as usual:

2. I don't really get this one. It's really easy to find any game you want using online. Be it a mascot platformer or anything else really (panty party anyone? Only pegi 7)

3. I haven't played any pikmin. And nothing about pikmin day made me want to check out the franchise more than i did before. But i do like the idea of these kinds of dates. Makes for a fun build up to it every year.

Gjang gjang-a-gjang-a-gjangGjang gjang-a-gjang-a-gjangGjang gjang-a-gjang-a-gjangGjang gjang-a-gjang-a-gjangwwWWWAAAAAAWAWAWA

Agree with GameMechanixz in the sense that big budget publishers seem to be falling into this trap more and more and forgetting what makes games fun in the first place (Sony and even the new GTA come to mind.) There is apparently a huge audience for it just like there is a huge audience for big budget superhero movies and such. I’ll stick with Nintendo and, as others mentioned, smaller and more experimental studios, too.

@JohnnyMind Yeah but do you want a pok or not??

@LimitedPower Ha ha, of course I want a Pok, too!

My thoughts on each letter: 1. A great story and glad you got to play OoT! What a great mom.

Games that are based off of movies (007, Indiana Jones, etc) should obviously keep their main characters and a life sim like GTA wouldn’t make sense with a dog protagonist but I would still prefer non-human, more creative characters over regular human ones (excluding Mario of course😉).

You could risk a ban by auto-uploading GTA 6 clips to the Xbox Network

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

If you're playing GTA 6 on Xbox, you should turn off your console's automatic upload feature or you could risk having your Xbox account suspended. An Xbox user on Reddit reported receiving a two-day, unrepealable ban for automatically uploading a 28-second clip of GTA 6 characters at the beach. According to the Reddit user, sangobar, the clip was almost immediately flagged by the Xbox Network for either violating the Xbox Community Standards or Microsoft Services Agreement terms (the email they received from Xbox doesn't specify which). However, the user claims the clip only showed characters in beachwear and the clip was therefore incorrectly flagged.So, to avoid the risk of an Xbox ban it is better to be safe than sorry, to disable your Xbox automatic upload feature, and to understand what Xbox's guidelines are around the content you can upload to the Xbox Network.

Automatic uploads to the Xbox Network are enabled as standard on Xbox, meaning the GTA 6 clips you capture on your console are automatically uploaded to the Xbox Network. To turn off your Xbox Series X's automatic uploads feature, follow these steps:

One Drive is more lenient in what you can upload, but if you'd rather not automatically upload any of your GTA 6 capture, it's best to set both it and Xbox Network to 'Don't Upload'.

GTA 6 clips could potentially violate the 'Keep your content clean' term of the Xbox Community Standards, specifically the 'Make stuff that's suitable for all audiences rule', which states: "The Xbox community must be friendly and accessible to everyone, this isn't the appropriate place for sexual content. Keep your public posts and messages suitable for all ages and audiences."

According to Xbox, some examples of content that could violate this term include sharing or distributing non-consensual intimate imagery, links or imagery that displays pornography, screenshots or game clips that include mature sexual content, custom gamerpics that contains nudity, lewd messages to other players, and distasteful or inappropriate pictures. In other words, be careful before sharing images or clips of GTA 6's more mature content, like GTA 6 strip clubs.

#3975. Three Games Are Confirmed For Xbox Game Pass To End The Month (November 24-27)

Here's what's on the way to close out the month

With only a handful of days left to go, November is well and truly coming to a close. Before we whip out the Xmas deccies, we've still got another three Xbox Game Pass titles to come over the next few days.

Starting off with XGP Premium members being treated to not just one, but two new additions to the mid-tier subscription. MOTORSLICE is making the move from Ultimate, whilst Sniper Ghost Warrior Contracts 2 is joining all but Essential on November 24.

The only "day one" game is coming just three days later, when Arkheron, a "fast-paced, clip-worthy team PvP game" joins Ultimate and PC Game Pass. It looks like a vibrant one if MOBAs are your cuppa.

Admittedly, it's a bit of a quiet end to November, but we'll leave you with a closer look at each of these games below.

On this page: Three Games Are Confirmed For Xbox Game Pass To End The Month (November 24-27)

Parkour through the ruins of a megastructure, climb massive bosses, and hunt down every construction equipment in this slice of life action-adventure with immaculate vibes.

Sniper Ghost Warrior Contracts 2 now includes ‘Butcher’s Banquet’: a major expansion which introduces an entirely new and expansive region - The Temple - complete with all-new objectives and some of your most deadly contracts, yet.

Arkheron is a fast-paced, clip-worthy team PvP game where the items you equip dynamically change how you play. Grab your friends, loot Relics that change your build mid-fight, and climb a haunted Tower floor by floor. If you've played a shooter or a MOBA, your aim and your instincts already work here. The builds, the counters, the hundred ways a fight can turn all boils down to your adaptability and skill.

#3974. Feature: A Lost Box Restored My Faith In Zelda's Staying Power

A few weeks ago, my brother sent me a photo with zero context. He was at our parents’ house, helping them pack up for a cross-country move, when he found something unusual: a heavy metal box with a latch.

It took me a second to dust off the cobwebs in that corner of my mind, but once I did, I recognised the box as the promotional material Nintendo sent me back in 1998 to celebrate the original release of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time.

I asked my bro what was inside the box and a few moments later he replied with another picture. The box was empty.

I can’t think of anything more depressing than an empty treasure chest. All the anticipation leading to… crushing disappointment. Anyone who ever slogged through the Phoenix Cave in Final Fantasy VI knows the feeling.

This chest originally housed a pre-launch, gold N64 cart of Ocarina of Time. It was Nintendo’s not-so-subtle message that this game was a treasure. A bit on the nose, but the zeitgeist of an entire generation of gamers has certainly proven them right. OoT is a treasure.

In this case, I can at least take solace knowing that I'm the one who emptied the chest and thoroughly enjoyed its golden treasure. The empty box is evidence of that.

My brother’s timing was impeccable — bordering on eerie — unearthing the box less than a week before the Switch 2 remake launched.

Like many of you, my son (let's call him Tim) and I were eagerly awaiting the OoT remake. He hadn’t played the original, but is an avid Zelda fan, particularly the modern titles. I knew I’d love the Remake, but I was a bit nervous that he would have a different reaction. He’s a member of this Breath of the Wild, open-world generation, after all. Would the old-school Zelda formula appeal to his generation, or would it die with mine?

As they say, sometimes one man’s treasure is another man’s trash.

My love for Zelda, and desire to pass it down to my son, parallels the experience my father had with his four boys. Dad loved to work with his hands and my brothers and I were always enlisted in projects: everything from clearing the land, felling trees, reroofing the house, building an addition, repainting, and working on a long series of rundown cars. He made sure we received hands-on working experience.

Right around the time I received the Zelda Treasure Chest, my dad began restoring classic Ford Mustangs in his garage. I had already moved out, but my youngest brother ( the one who found the chest) was there to be Dad’s understudy. Together they restored two beautiful Mustangs, allowing my dad to share his love for mechanical craft and manual labour.

Sharing an old classic is one thing, but actually passing down a passion depends on how well the original holds up to modern sensibilities.

A restored car regains its iconic look, but it will also retain the old feel, complete with stiff brakes and crank windows. After all, restoring something doesn’t place it in a state opposite to its nature. A 1967 Mustang GT Fastback is a 1967 Mustang GT Fastback only if it looks, sounds, and feels like a 1967 Mustang GT Fastback, for better or worse.

Media remakes and remasters are often criticised for following this type of approach. Shot-for-shot remakes come across as unnecessary cash grabs (looking at you Disney) while complete reimaginings seem to either spectacularly succeed (Dune, Casino Royale, Metroid Zero Mission) or fail (Planet of the Apes 2001, Secret of Mana, Quantum Leap).

Like my old man, Nintendo’s philosophy seems closer to restoration than reimagining. Star Fox and Super Mario RPG are recent examples, with the slightly more ambitious Link’s Awakening preceding them by a few years. There are many others.

In each case, the spirit of the original is preserved while a few quality-of-life improvements are added. And of course, each old classic receives a new coat of paint.

By taking this approach, Nintendo has been careful to avoid the pitfalls that so many media companies encounter when updating beloved products. Their roster of remakes have largely avoided any 'Han shot first' controversies. Thank goodness.

A philosophy of preserving the original’s frame, while souping up the engine, allows old and new players to enjoy the gaming experience without fighting retro clunkiness.

So, what does Tim think of Ocarina of Time?

He loves it, of course! And it’s been immensely satisfying to see him enjoy it. Confirmation bias can be a wonderful thing.

The wife and I have a ritual of playing Zelda games together, so we’re playing it in short, infrequent bursts. I’m not complaining, as it’s allowed me to savour the experience. Tim, on the other hand, is powering through it at a much faster pace. He also spectates while my wife and I play. We always aim for a 100% run, so Tim takes notes on all of the heart pieces and bag upgrades he missed.

I’m just excited to see my son enjoying a game I grew up with. My dad passed on his love for mechanical craft to his boys, and I’m sharing my passion for sidequests with mine.

It’s been a good month. It began with a nostalgic relic and a bit of disappointment (grr, I still can’t find that gold cart), but also included a timeless masterpiece that’s been successfully passed to the next generation.

30 years ago my dad shared the muscle cars from his youth. This year I got to share a classic Zelda adventure from mine.

I wonder what treasure my boy will pass on to his kids in 30 years' time.

Have you successfully passed a favourite game down to the next generation? Was it the original, or a remake that added modern improvements? Share your stories in the comments below.

#3973. Guide: GTA 6: How to Get Ultimate Edition Items & Pre-Order Bonuses

GTA 6's Ultimate Edition features a collection of different items and pre-order bonuses, including vehicles, weapons, and cosmetics. These are unlocked at different points in the story, and some need to be collected from locations around the map. This GTA 6 guide includes step-by-step instructions on how to collect them and when they become available.

On this page: GTA 6: How to Get Ultimate Edition Items & Pre-Order Bonuses

There are 15 extra packs included if you pre-ordered GTA 6's Ultimate Edition. This is where you find them:

You'll find the Dinka Enduro motorcycle and Crest Kayak around Jason's House in Key Lento, Mariana County. They're marked on the map, as shown below:

Here's the Dinka Enduro motorcycle underneath Jason's house:

The Crest Kayak is then at the bottom of the ramp leading into the water:

You can also equip a custom Retro livery to Jason's Vapid Ganado by taking it to any Mod Shop, like Coastal Auto Care. Here's what the Retro livery looks like; you'll find it under Pro Builds > Full Kits > Retro Build - Ultimate Edition:

These items are only available in Chapter 1.

An early mission in Chapter 1 will see you go to an Ammu-Nation to purchase a new weapon. Having done so, the Duval Signature ES9 Variant will unlock in the nearby Weapon Locker.

Here's where the mission will take you on the map, with the Duval Signature ES9 Variant for Jason first found there:

The Electric Fang Tattoo Parlor is located on Coral Ave, Stockyard, Vice City, Vice-Dale County from Chapter 1. Here's how it looks from the outside:

You can set a waypoint under the tabs Style > Tattoos:

Many of the items here are Ultimate Edition exclusive, and marked with a blue tab in the top-right corner:

The Goodtime Gear items can be purchased beginning Chapter 1 at The Wonder Whale shop on Sunbelt Hwy, Key Lento, Mariana County. This is how it looks from the outside:

Here's the location on your map. You can also set a marker to the exact store by selecting the Style > Souvenir & Swimwear tabs, as below:

You'll find the Goodtime Gear items inside the shop, on mannequins just left of the entrance:

The Ultimate Edition exclusive items are marked with a blue tab, as shown:

You can find One-Eyed Willie's Auto Shop just off SR-27 in North Leonard County starting from Chapter 1. It looks like this from the outside:

And here's a map view to help direct you to the right spot:

You can set a waypoint using the menu tabs Vehicles > Mod Shops:

Drive in to the mod shop to find exclusive paint jobs and body work, many of which are exclusive to the Ultimate Edition:

You'll need to have visited South Vice-Dale County before the PTT Youngin$ Illegal Goods robberies unlock starting from Chapter 1. Once you have, you'll find two robberies in and around SW 13th St and El Joven Blvd in Southside.

You can set a waypoint directly to them from the Robberies > Illegal Operations tab in your map:

Take out the gang members inside and loot all the jewelry and drugs before the police arrive:

Then make a quick getaway in your vehicle:

Remember to stow the stolen goods and take them to a nearby fence for cash:

The Rideout Custom Mod Shop is located in Crosstown, Vice City, Vice-Dale County. Here's what it looks like outside:

Note that it's marked with an Ultimated Edition symbol. It can be found under the Vehicles > Mod Shops tab of the map menu:

Take your car here to customise it with all kinds of specialty rims and interiors. Items exclusive to the Rideout Custom Mod Shop will be marked:

You can visit Sara's Unisex Salon from Chapter 1, but Signature styles will not unlock until Chapter 2. Here's what the shop looks like:

And here's its location on your map, which can be found under the Style > Hair & Beauty tab. It's located on Cicada Ave, Hamlet, South Vice-Dale County, Vice-Dale County:

Ultimate Edition exclusive items are marked with a blue tab in the top-right corner:

Stock 305 can be access on NE 15th St, Stockyard, Vice City, Vice-Dale County from Chapter 1. It looks like this from the outside:

You can find it with the map tabs by selecting Style > Casual & Street:

Inside you'll find Ultimate Edition exclusive clothes for both Jason and Lucia:

You'll get a notification as you progress through Chapter 2 that your '67 Dominator Buggy is available to collect from your Paradise garage, which looks like this:

The Paradise garage is in Watson Bay, Mariana County. Here's its location on your map just in case you get lost:

Get inside the '67 Dominator Buggy to register it. Any current cars you're using will be sent back to one of your other garages automatically:

You'll also unlock some liveries for the '67 Dominator Buggy you can access by taking it to any Pay 'n' Spray.

Shortly after collecting your '67 Vapid Dominator, you'll receive a text message on your phone from Wyman telling you about a classic car you can recover and tune up.

This triggers a new chain of missions where you must scan scrap cars for Wyman to repair.

You can find Wyman's Classic Car Locations through the link.

Go to any Ammunation store around Leonidas and select Manage Weapons at the Weapon Locker, like below:

From Chapter 2 onwards, you'll find the Hawk & Little Morgan in the Revolvers section of both Jason and Lucia's Weapon Locker:

Your Vintage Vice City Pack pre-order bonus will become available shortly after you arrive in Vice City. A marker will appear on your map telling you to visit the familiar Ocean View Hotel in Vice Beach, telling you to pick up your '55 Vapid Stanier, which can be located like below:

The car is unlocked, and once you get inside you'll automatically receive the Shore Court garage as well as new clothes in your wardrobe. A prompt will inform you of this:

You'll also find new hairstyles and more in the Special tab at salons as well as various gun liveries at Ammunation, marked with the Vintage Vice City Pack label:

You can collect your Shitzu Squalo beginning Chapter 4, docked near to Atlantic Ave, Washington Beach, Vice Beach, Vice-Dale County. Here's where you'll find it:

Here's a map view. It's just east of the Y Hotel:

You will find it on the Personal section of your map tabs, but only when you're in a nearby area:

Once you've made progress in Chapter 4, items from the Vice City Style items will be automatically added to your Wardrobe and the Special tab of of most hair salons and tattoo parlours, as below:

You'll get a notification about the '95 Grotti Cheetah upon completing Honest Abe in Chapter 5. Follow the waypoint to Pegassi Residences and go through the main front door, as shown:

Go inside the main entrance and use the lift opposite the entrance:

Your '95 Grotti Cheetah will be parked up and waiting for you to get inside:

GTA 6's Ultimate Edition costs $99.99/£89.99/€99.99. The Standard Edition costs $79.99/£69.99/€79.99.

Yes, I personally think GTA 6's Ultimate Edition is worth it, but it really depends how excited you are for the game and whether you want to get the most out of it.

All of the additional Mod Shops and Stores exclusive to the Ultimate Edition, along with their unique inventory, means you're really adding a lot of cosmetic and personalisation options to the title with the Ultimate Edition.

If you're not the type of player that plans to dress up Jason and Lucia and fiddle with their vehicles, then you may not find value in this.

But it's worth adding that the Classic Car Collection, which adds collectibles quests involving Wyman, are also exclusive to the Ultimate Edition.

You can still enjoy GTA 6 to its fullest without paying for the Ultimate Edition, but you'll get much more out of the game if you do.

Yes, the Ultimate Edition Upgrade can be purchased from the PS Store at any time for $20.00/£20.00/€20.00 and will automatically add all of the extra content to your game once installed.

You'll need to buy the Ultimate Edition Upgrade if you purchase a physical edition of GTA 6, as this content isn't included with the retail release.

If you've followed this guide carefully, then you should now have collected all of your Ultimate Edition items and pre-order bonuses in GTA 6. Congratulations for getting them all!

Remember, you can refer to our GTA 6 guide for a lot more info on the game, including collectibles, walkthroughs, and much more.

If you want to move faster in Grand Theft Auto 6, I can't blame you: There's a lot I've enjoyed about the opening hours I've spent in Jason's shoes. He's handy with a nailgun. He's a good sport when I make him wear the dumbest graphic tees I can find. For a gunslinging drug runner, he's a gentle soul. I just have one complaint.

The man's got a leisurely gait. Which is fine! But there are plenty of times while roaming Leonida when you might wish he and Lucia were moving just a bit faster—just not so fast that you want to force them into a run. Luckily, Rockstar's got our back: There's a setting to bump up your basic movement speed without pushing a button.

To change the pace that Jason and Lucia move at in GTA 6, head to Settings, move over to the Gameplay tab, and scroll down to the Movement section. The setting you're looking for is Movement Speed.

This doesn't affect your top speed while sprinting and burning stamina. What it adjusts is the speed you move at when you fully push the joystick. There are four options, each one offering more speed than the last: Walk (the default), Fast Walk, Jog, and Run.

It's a nice bit of granularity. I go with Fast Walk to give just a slight bump in my base speed without feeling like I'm rushing, but Jog or Run are good options if you really want to cover ground. Whichever one you choose, you can still voluntarily move at a slower pace by only slightly tilting the joystick.

There's also a Combat Movement Speed setting, which—as you might expect—changes the pace you walk at in a gunfight. There are only three options here: Fast Walk, Jog, and Run, because nobody wants to move slowly when they're actively being shot at.

While you're in the menus, I'd recommend digging around to inspect all the available options. Rockstar included a lot of toggles and tweaks for fine-tuning how GTA 6 handles. You can even turn off vehicle damage altogether, if you don't want to pay for car repairs. Not that I've ever crashed or anything. Don't ask my mechanic.
