Finding the Slim Jim in Chapter 2 is essential if you want to get better at stealing vehicles

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Stealing cars in GTA 6 is one of the easiest ways to attract attention from the police, thanks to the new Wanted system. You've probably noticed by now that breaking into vehicles is noisy and messy, with Jason and Lucia needing to smash the window to get inside. It also takes time – precious time in which some nosey onlooker can report your description and activity to the cops. There has to be an easier way, right? There is. Which is why you need to learn how to get a Slim Jim in GTA 6.

The Slim Jim in GTA 6 is only available from Chapter 2 onwards. This essential carjacking tool will unlock as part of the main GTA 6 mission list, coming into your possession after you begin a quest called 'Moses'. It's in this mission where you'll meet your first vehicle fence, learn how to sell cars and bikes in GTA 6, and be given the information you need to better survey vehicles for security features with the WAiNK app – which can be activated at any time by holding Up on the D-pad.

Moses will give you the Slim Jim as a part of this mission. It'll let you get into any vehicle without needing to smash the window. You will, however, still need to contend with security features – you'll have to wait until Chapter 3 to learn how to get the Key Cloner in GTA 6 and understand how to deactivate trackers to steal more modern vehicles.

Once you've got it, using the Slim Jim is GTA 6 is easy enough. Walk up to any vehicle you want to try and steal. Walk up to the driver-side or passenger door, and press Triangle/Y to bring out your Slim Jim. From there, it's a case of rotating the right thumbstick in a curve until you find the sweet spot – which you'll spot by rumble in the controller and by a slightly pink hue to the semi-circle indicator. Eventually you'll hear a little pop, meaning you can now climb inside.

#3970. GTA 6 Glitch Unlocks The FPS On Xbox Series X|S, But With Multiple Drawbacks

It's a bug related to Quick Resume on Series X|S

If there's anything we could add to GTA 6 as things stand, it'd be an official 60FPS mode. That's obviously not possible right now due to how demanding the game is on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S hardware, even in the case of the PS5 Pro.

Interestingly though, over the weekend, players have discovered the ability to activate what some are calling a "60FPS Glitch" or "60FPS Bug" on Xbox consoles, forcing the game to unlock its FPS and run at a higher frame rate than it's actually supposed to.

Someone called Meowwie64 on Reddit appears to have found this, and here's what they did to activate it:

Now, as mentioned, there are multiple drawbacks here. The first one is that the glitch speeds up most aspects of the game, making it run faster than intended (and look like it's in fast-forward mode!). This is obviously not an ideal way to enjoy GTA 6, and serves as an immediate deal-breaker in my view.

Another one is that reaching 60FPS is pretty much impossible under normal gameplay circumstances. If you're driving down a highway, for example, you're likely only going to get around 35-40FPS at max, with 60FPS and above being saved for situations that require no graphical intensity whatsoever.

And finally, it should be noted that GTA 6 was never intended to be run this way on Xbox Series X|S, and therefore you could run into all sorts of issues - crashes, bugs, maybe even your console overheating. That last one is unlikely, but the game has been specifically built to run at 30FPS on these machines, so it's not worth pushing it in our view.

We'll leave you with some footage of this glitch running on Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S down below (courtesy of the always-excellent Fuzion Xbox Testing), and prepare for it to be officially fixed in an upcoming GTA 6 update.

I can’t wait to hear stories of other people’s adventures. I’ll share an insane situation I had last night - I was driving to a rundown RV park in the backwoods to confront some people. As I was making my way there I saw a dead and bloodied dear lying on the rough and rocky terrain. As I drove a little closer, this beast, which was Bigfoot, was eating the dear but got startled by my presence. I got out of my car and chased it through the woods but I lost its tail.

As I’m running through the thicket of bushes, weeds, swampy alligators, and muddy landscape, I hear gunshots in the distance. I go to investigate. That’s when I stumbled upon a rundown hotel. There was a wide open door, and a man was crawling outside bleeding. Inside, there was another man screaming. He was being attacked by a tiger in his hotel room. I shoot the tiger dead, and the two other men succumb to their wounds.

All of this noise must have attracted other scumbags because as I was looting the room that had cash, drugs, and some weapons (one being a flare gun), I get ambushed. I quickly pulled out my weapon, not realizing I upholstered said flare gun, and began shooting the people after me. They caught on fire, and one of the men ran nearby a vehicle which ultimately exploded. I quickly get my bearings, loot the area, and find a 4-wheeler that I steal, and I take off like a bat out of hell.

This whole encounter was a random event that I just so happened to witness and take part of. The level of detail, writing, and interactivity is mind blowing. It is a perfect example as to why Rockstar is the best at what they do. It’s an insane event that can only happen in the worlds Rockstar creates.

Looks like Lawrence Sullivan settled his differences with Rockstar.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Remember in the closing days of 2023, when Rockstar dropped the first trailer for Grand Theft Auto 6? Amidst the everything it had going on was a brief shot of a man with extensive facial tattoos, who was quickly called out by people hip to such things as a knockoff of Florida Joker, aka Lawrence Sullivan, a Florida man who went viral for his 2017 mug shot.

Sullivan himself called it out in a since-deleted TikTok video, first telling Rockstar "we gotta talk" and then, with no response forthcoming, threatening legal action. Not long after that, though, he put forth a new offer: "Let me voice the character, give me more storyline in the game… Let's make history happen, man."

It seems that Sullivan got what he wanted: In a video posted to Instagram, Sullivan said he was given a role in GTA 6.

"I'm an official voice actor on GTA 6, the game." Sullivan says. "For the last three years a lot of people were saying I was not going to be in the game, I was not going to be nothing, they were destroying my mental health. They were saying a lot of fucked shit. But now it's time for me to shit on them and show them what the fuck Florida Joker is about!"

"Y'all gonna see. Special voice actor for GTA 6. This ain't no gimmick, this ain't no lie!"

A post shared by Florida joker 🃏 (@floridaajoker)

I had doubts, but this apparently really ain't no gimmick or lie. Rockstar has posted the full GTA 6 credits and sure enough, Lawrence Sullivan is in there. Now, it could be a different Lawrence Sullivan, sure, but under the circumstances I don't think that's very likely.

Sullivan's role doesn't appear to be a particularly prominent one: He's credited, along with a great many other people, as one of "The Local Population." But at the end of the day, he made it: Florida Joker really is in GTA 6, and he seems pretty chuffed about it. I'd call that a happy ending.

#3967. Ubisoft lays off 166 staff at Montreal and Quebec studios

Ubisoft has laid off 166 staff across its Ubisoft Montreal and Ubisoft Quebec studios, the company announced.

“Ubisoft is reducing its workforce by 166 positions across its Montreal and Quebec City operations,” a Ubisoft spokesperson said in a statement. “As our portfolio evolves, our production needs are changing, requiring us to adjust the size of some teams to ensure our resources are aligned with current production priorities and business needs.”

The spokesperson continued, “We deeply value the contributions of these teams and recognize the impact this may have on our colleagues. We are committed to supporting them through this process with care and respect. Those affected are being provided with severance, extended health care benefits, career transition services and other resources.”

A source told IGN that the layoffs affect employees whose projects have been canceled or refocused, as well as those who could not be reassigned due to the decrease in the number of active projects.

#3966. 61% of All US PS5 Owners Played GTA 6 on Launch Day, Averaging 8 Hours

You’ve seen the staggering 32.5 million pre-launch sales, but now enjoy some console specific data on GTA 6’s release.

Analyst Mat Piscatella of Circana reports that in the US, 61% of PS5 owners played Rockstar’s latest release on launch day. That’s an utterly astounding statistic.

But here’s the really staggering part – said players averaged about 8.5 hours of gameplay on 19th November. Averaged!

According to Circana's Player Engagement Tracker, Grand Theft Auto VI had a massive launch (surprise!). For players active on November 19th, 61% of US PlayStation 5 and 56% of global Xbox players engaged with Grand Theft Auto VI. PS5 GTA VI players averaged 513 minutes that day, Xbox players 494.

That’s an utterly flabbergasting figure – I almost can’t believe it. I’d love to know the impact on global productivity, as I’m sure anecdotally we all know someone who took a sick day.

Anyway, this is jaw-dropping data and I’m sure there’s a lot more to come.

Credit to Sony, by the way, who’s kept the PS5 online and running flawlessly throughout this enormous influx of traffic. Preload went smoothly, and I haven’t really seen anyone complaining they had issues this week.

At the risk of coming off as pedantic I have to also chime in that the headline and resultant assumptions here are misleading. It’s does clarify in the article (although many passersby will just see the headline). Basically it’s not that 61% of PS5’s are playing GTA, it’s that of the PS5’s online and connected to the PSN that day (launch day) 61% of those were engaged with GTA6. By engaged with, it could mean that they played the game and maybe it also could mean that it was just downloaded… it’s not clear. So there’s plenty of PS5’s and players (like myself) who didn’t turn on their PS5 on Nov 19th. Some of us went to work that day and haven’t bought GTA yet, so obviously our consoles were off.

It’s just another example of skewed statistics, or rather, taking an impressive number out of context to try to exaggerate a trend. We have seen these same statistical manipulations a lot during the disc debates.

The game is doing fantastic on its own and is a triumph, no doubt. We don’t need to inflate the numbers. 61% of all PS5’s are not playing GTA6

#3964. GTA 6's narrative lead says Jason's reserved demeanor was inspired by a 1972 crime movie

"So many of our protagonists have been the opposite."

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

One half of GTA 6's leading couple, Jason Duval, is unusually reserved and soft-spoken when compared to many of the crime series' boisterous, sometimes gleefully violent protagonists. Why the change? Rockstar Games' narrative lead says the idea came from 1972's The Getaway and Jason's military background.

"When we decided we wanted to tell a story about a couple on the run, we looked at all the similar kinds of movies, and one of the ones that really stood out was [Sam] Peckinpah's The Getaway," senior vice president of narrative, Rupert Humphries, says in a statement given to Destructoid.

The crime flick's star Steve McQueen "was famous for pulling lines out of scripts and saying things with his presence alone," Humphries continues, and that's an energy the team at Rockstar wanted to somewhat match with Jason's characterisation. Although, he also acknowledges that "so many of our protagonists have been the opposite." Think Trevor and the like.

"This also resonated with the research we were doing around veterans and particularly former Army Rangers (in our world we call them Marauders). These guys typically aren't running their mouths or reacting to something unless it's strictly necessary, while still being strong and still asserting themselves," Humphries adds.

The game itself definitely plays on those ideas, too. (Something noted in our GTA 6 review.) Jason isn't the most forthcoming or chatty protagonist, but what he leaves unsaid and when he chooses to communicate is just as important as what he actually shares with Lucia - the other, more chaotic half of the game's central couple, who balances things out somewhat.

"Researching the prolific and headline-grabbing criminal activity that had been taking place over decades in Florida was an obvious starting point," game writer Michael Wiafe also said of the game's sweeping story. "From then on, it was about coming up with authentic characters that didn't stray too far from reality but also were not totally bound by it either. The majority of our main characters are undeniably reprehensible on paper, full-blown criminals, but also decent human beings. Their moral makeup isn't necessarily cut-and-dry, and we don't attempt to make excuses for them. What's important is how they resonate, no matter where you're experiencing the game in the world."

GTA 6's map is so big it's going to take months for people to comb through it and find everything. Rockstar has already posted the full map of Leonida online, but it doesn't answer one simple question that I know we've all been wondering: How long would it take to fly across this entire thing in a plane?

The answer is a lot less time than it would take to go by car, but still long enough to give you an idea of the sheer scale we're working with here. Using the closest plane to Jason's house, my trip across Leonida took around 4 minutes and 18 seconds, which is a little under an hour of in-game time. You can watch the entire flight from start to finish below.

Keep in mind that the Mammoth Dodo seaplane that carried me from the southern tip of the archipelago to the northern tip of the map is just one type of plane in GTA 6. I would bet there are faster options if you really want to zoom.

Even though I'm still very early in the GTA 6's story, I didn't have to go too far out of my way to test this. Jason's house is conveniently located pretty close to a spot with perfectly unattended planes to borrow. The Sunbelt Highway that runs south of it will lead you right to the earliest planes and helicopters you can find. Just don't fly over the nearby military base (trust me, it's bad news) and you'll be fine.

Rockstar compared GTA 6's map to its previous games, describing it as about the size of GTA 4, GTA 5, and Red Dead Redemption 2 combined. Despite knowing this beforehand, I was still shocked to see how the map kept going when I first opened it up. Four minutes might not sound like a lot, but the enormity of it all sinks in as you glide above densely populated cities and neighborhoods that could be the setting of their own standalone videogames.

My experiment has left the fog of war on my map split into two halves. My flight path carved a line of partially revealed locations straight through it. I don't expect to clear the rest out for dozens of hours, but now I'm tempted to find out how long of a roadtrip it would be to do the same journey by car.

#3959. Rockstar wants you to see yourself in GTA 6's Jason and Lucia

"We might all be better off when we're together and not going it alone."

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

GTA 6's Jason and Lucia might be hardened criminals, but Rockstar Games designed the couple to be relatable in other ways. As the studio's narrative lead explained, "we are all about two bits of bad luck away from completely losing it" in the real world.

"Playing GTA 6, the main thing we want players to feel is connection. To Jason and Lucia, who they need to believe in and inhabit for this journey through the game, but then also that connection in the game between the two characters," senior vice president of narrative, Rupert Humphries, explained in quotes given to GamesRadar+.

"Living in the actual world in this present moment, it feels like there is so much noise and so much pressure on everyone - politics, the environment, media, social media. It's coming at you from everywhere. It seems like we are all about two bits of bad luck away from completely losing it. That is the world we are showing you on the streets of Vice City and in the rest of Leonida - everyone's been driven to a kind of madness that comes out in lots of different ways, from conspiracy theories to self-help cults to get-rich-quick schemes and drug habits."

GTA 6's main couple doesn't exactly have many options outside of the criminal ones, and I think the game does a good job at giving them some real, personal, human stakes to ground it all - making their occasional robberies and murders a tad more understandable. As the couple says in the game, the world is stacked against them. They can't get ahead by playing by the rules.

Even so, GTA 6 still has an optimistic view on life in the modern era, which itself is a big departure from GTA 5's generally cynical world view: "With all that going on, we wanted to have two humans at the center of the story that the player can care about and see themselves in, and then this idea that maybe (however bad you are) we might all be better off when we're together and not going it alone."

You can check our GTA 6 guide to see how to make the most of Jason and Lucia's relationship, or read our GTA 6 review if you're still on the fence.

#3958. Saihate Station: Twilight Edition announced for Switch

Publisher PLAYISM and developer viv have announced Saihate Station: Twilight Edition, a Switch version of the 2D exploration horror adventure game including the base game and downloadable content “Twilight Railway,” as well as two mini-games. It will launch on March 25, 2027 worldwide with English, Japanese, Korean, Traditional Chinese, and Simplified Chinese language support. A physical edition will be available in Japan for 8,800 yen.

Saihate Station first launched for PC via Steam on March 7, 2025. The downloadable content “Twilight Railway” launched on April 18, 2025.

Here is an overview of the game, via PLAYISM:

Since its release in March 2025, this 2D exploration horror adventure game has recorded a cumulative series total of 1.6 million downloads, an exceptional achievement for an indie free game, and continues to receive passionate support from fans in Japan and abroad. Now it is finally coming to Nintendo Switch!

Saihate Station: Twilight Edition includes the main game, the downloadable content “Twilight Railway,” and two mini-games, all in one package.

“After falling asleep on the last train, I woke up in a bizarre place called Saihate Station…”

Haru Akinashi is a self-effacing office worker who lacks confidence and fails at everything he tries. Having slept through his stop on the last train, he finds himself trapped in a bizarre place called Saihate Station, where gruesome supernatural phenomena occur.

Shion Tatsunami is his complete opposite: a cheerful, talented colleague and former friend—happens to be there as well, and the two promise to work together to return home.

Their interactions are awkward at first, given the estrangement, but with each problem they overcome together, Haru recalls their former friendship, and their bond grows stronger than before.

The main game features four multiple-ending story routes. The ending branches based on fluctuations in Haru’s “dependency level,” which changes according to the player’s actions.

Starting November 20, pre-orders for the physical edition will begin sequentially at retailers in Japan. As a first-print bonus, a “shaka-shaka acrylic stand keychain” featuring a train and character motif will be included. A limited edition featuring a special box with an “exclusive newly drawn mini-game book” and a “Haru-Shion handkerchief” is also planned. Bonuses and limited editions are available in limited quantities, so please place your pre-order early.

#3957. PS5 Survives GTA 6's Unfathomably Humongous Launch without a Hitch

We’d rightly criticise Sony if the PS5 had fallen to pieces during GTA 6’s launch, so let’s give the platform holder a nod of approval for navigating these past two weeks almost flawlessly.

There were some minor scattered instances of PSN outages on Wednesday evening prior to the Rockstar title’s big launch, but these never affected everyone and the network recovered pretty fast. I think we can give that a pass.

Meanwhile, the preload process worked flawlessly as far as I’m aware. I haven’t really seen any widespread reporting of people being unable to download the game in advance of its release.

Given its size and the sheer number of people wanting to play – remember, 32.5 million copies were sold across all consoles prior to release – that’s a humongous strain on Sony’s servers, which is predicted to have accounted for approximately 75% of all purchases.

Obviously GTA 6 is a single player-only game, so that certainly put less stress on the PSN as a whole, and the new GTA Online’s eventual launch will be an even bigger test – but for now, the PS5 has held up remarkably well.

I’m not saying we should get out the champagne – this is the experience consumers quite rightly expect Sony to deliver.

But this was still a huge, unprecedented test for PlayStation’s infrastructure – and it’s fair to say it navigated it almost flawlessly. In my opinion, that deserves acknowledging at least.

#3956. Tripwire Interactive says it's laying off 36 staff in a "necessary" decision, while reassuring that Killing Floor 3 and Maneater 2 are still in active development

In a statement posted yesterday, Killing Floor developers Tripwire Interactive have announced that the studio is laying off 36 "talented" internal staff as part of a "workforce reduction". The job cuts come 16 months after the release of Killing Floor 3 (which James didn't care for), and within hours of unrelated yet equally dispiriting redunancies at Skydance Games.

Tripwire's announcement claims that this was "not an easy decision, but unfortunately a necessary one for the organisation," adding that "these are truly great people who are exceptional at their roles, and we will help support these individuals with compassion and dignity during this transition." There's a small hope in me that this might mean helping those affected find new jobs quickly, though it's hard to stay optimistic when mass layoffs in games development have become such a regular occurrence.

Despite this post primarily being about the loss of 36 livelihoods, Tripwire are quick to reassure fans that Killing Floor 3's post-launch updates remain in active development, as does their comedy shark-action sequel Maneater 2. The studio "remain committed to our awesome community", they say; apparently just not to their awesome employees.

This news also arrives just days after Tripwire expanded its publishing business to support small indie developers, and less than a year after its last round of layoffs in March. Tripwire also happens to have been acquired by layoff extraordinaire corporation Embracer in 2022, just for some relevant context.

#3955. Witch on the Holy Night now available for iOS, Android in Japan

Publisher Aniplex and developer TYPE-MOON have released visual novel Witch on the Holy Night for iOS via App Store and Android via Google Play in Japan for 2,900 yen.

Witch on the Holy Night has previously been released for PlayStation 4, Switch, and PC via Steam. Shipments and digital sales have surpassed 500,000 units worldwide.

The mobile release coincides with the Witch on the Holy Night anime movie produced by ufotable, which debuted in Japanese theaters today.

Here is an overview of the game, via Aniplex:

Experience a young adult tale, set in the vibrant and bustling 1980s, that follows an innocent young man and two young “witches.”

Updates added since the original PC version include the fully voiced characters that fans have long awaited, as well as visuals remastered in full HD, bringing the experience to life with unparalleled image quality.

Various new visual elements not only imbue battle scenes with tension, but also breathe life into the characters’ everyday activities, with motions that bring a sense of animation and make the text even more deeply immersive.

Two witches dwell within a mansion atop a hill.

It is the late 1980s, the twilight years of a vibrant and bustling era. A boy arrives in the city only to encounter two witches living in the present day.

The boy leads a normal life. One of the girls is proud and dignified. The other lives hidden away, as if in slumber.

Three stars in parallel orbit, fated never to meet. The story of how these three completely different characters come to live under one roof will soon be revealed…

First released in 2012 for PC, Witch on the Holy Night returns after 10 years, further refined with fully voiced characters and a full high-definition visual remaster.

The company says its new generative AI training agreement will only be used for good. Why would anyone believe that?

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Online marketplace Etsy, best known as a platform for selling handmade goods, recently updated its user agreement to allow itself to "develop, train, test and improve artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies" using content uploaded by sellers.

This has not gone over well, with some closing their Etsy shops in protest. In response, Etsy has assured users that it doesn't plan to train AI systems designed to copy their work or replace their creativity. Instead, the company said that the change is about improving the platform and providing "services and tools that can help you run your business."

I am sometimes sympathetic toward companies that get yelled at for normal terms of service agreements. If a company hosts user-submitted content on the web, for instance, it needs a license to distribute that content globally, and sometimes users misunderstand that. This is not one of those cases.

The new agreement—which Etsy has told The New York Times it's planning to revise—says that Etsy and its third-party partners have the right to use uploaded content "to develop, train, test and improve artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies, including to improve the Services and/or help keep them safe."

That reads to me like blanket permission to train AI on user content for any purpose. The tacked-on note about keeping users safe does nothing to limit what Etsy can do.

The artists who sell cool custom keycaps and other fun things on Etsy are already likely to struggle against knock-off sellers if they get popular enough. That came with the territory of online selling even before AI, but it is absurd to now insist that they willingly hand over all the things that make their stores unique—their art, their product descriptions—to systems capable of duplicating those things in hard-to-trace ways, with only a pinky swear to protect them.

We've all seen how the AI industry has tried to brush off the concerns of artists and others whose work it ingests. One company went so far as to create a chatbot bearing the name of a former PC Gamer editor without permission, pretending that this robo-editor could give writing advice like the real person. And that's without him even knowing they were doing it!

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Even if Etsy truly does have good intentions, expecting artists to give this the thumbs up is ridiculous. It is not their responsibility to improve the platform by letting it mimic their creative work. The revised terms should, at the very least, exclude every seller from AI training as the default setting.

#3953. "A fight for all workers": SAG-AFTRA throw weight behind emerging Rockstar union ahead of its GTA 6 release week vote

In what has come to feel like the dawn of the final day before Grand Theft Auto VI's release, one thing that Rockstar really don't want people to be aware of is the ongoing legal dispute between the Rockstar Games Workers Union and the studio itself following Rockstar's alleged union busting in firing 31 union members last year. Starting on the 12th through to the 26th, recognition of the union will be voted upon by staff to ensure that workers would be given a say over "topics including pay and bonuses, overtime, redundancies, flexible working arrangements, and generative AI policies."

If it passes, the vote would also make the union the largest recognised union in the UK games industry, partly thanks to its partnership with the Independent Workers Union of Great Britain. Now, the global labor union SAG-AFTRA have chimed in to endorse the Workers Union, offering solidarity to the members involved and granting important leverage from a global force.

SAG-AFTRA's statement declares that "unionisation is vital for the future of the video game industry", and that "in the face of record layoffs, job instability, hostile work places, and toxic crunch culture, it is now more critical than ever for unions and workers to stand in support of one another." They advocate for fair treatment, especially in the wake of displacement due to corporate mismanagement and genAI, and proudly state that "this is a fight for all workers."

Their statement closes by saying that "the gaming industry is a commercial juggernaut, and the people that create these amazing works of art deserve fair treatment and the opportunity to improve the terms of their employment with a strong voice at the bargaining table. We honor the courage of our fellow game workers at Rockstar and proudly support their union vote."

Solidarity with the workers, always. We can only wait and see how the voting process pans out.

#3952. GTA 6 PS5 Review Bombing Out of Control as Zelda Receives Revenge Ratings

In response to a coordinated review bombing effort on GTA 6, fans of the Rockstar release appear to have launched a counter-attack on The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, believing Nintendo gamers are to blame for the situation.

Last night, I reported that GTA 6’s Metacritic user score was racking up ‘0’ review scores at an unprecedented pace. Many of the ratings were bogus.

In the hours since, the Switch 2’s universally adored remake of Ocarina of Time has seen its user score drop from 9.6 to 8.9 at the time of writing.

One ‘0’ rating simply reads: “Take your own medicine.”

At this point, I just wish Metacritic would do away with user scores, although I’ve no doubt this sorry situation is all good for business.

The thing is: this isn’t the first time the critic aggregator has become a battleground like this. As I mentioned in my original report, many of the greatest games ever made have pitiful user scores on the site.

Hopefully this all blows over, because it’s all rather embarrassing right now.

Original Story: GTA 6, the highest-rated game of all-time, is getting review bombed on Metacritic as idiots attempt to plunge the seminal Rockstar release’s rating with bogus ‘0’ scores.

At the time of writing, the title has a user score of 5.4, meaning it’s considered ‘Mixed or Average’:

This is in sharp contrast to critics, who awarded the game an average score of 99, making it the best-reviewed title of all time.

“Good thing Rockstar doesn’t blacklist user ratings like they do critics,” one review reads.

There’s a theory among some online that the dev blacklists media outlets for giving its games poor scores, but it put GTA 6 in the hands of more than 150 critics, so I don’t buy that for a single second.

Many of the ‘0’ reviews all touch on the same thing: 30fps is “unplayable”, the series has gone “woke”, and the “story is horrible”. (“I never smiled one time,” writes one seemingly perpetually miserable user.)

There are some legitimate criticisms among these; one person writes they’re not a fan of the life sim elements and prefer the “power fantasy” of older games. That’s fair, but it doesn’t make it a ‘0’.

Metacritic reviews have always been a disaster really, because you don’t need to actually own a game to rate it. Many of the best titles ever released have dreadful user scores on the site.

On the PS Store, though – where you actually have to spend money on the game to score it – the current rating sits at 4.84 based on 170k reviews. So that’s probably a better reflection of how the community feels.

My take on all this is that humans are predictable creatures: wherever there’s something popular, you’re probably going to find a group of people eager to tear it down.

@SpaceElf Nobody’s far enough along to really judge the story yet but the individual character development and world building so far is superb. That’s what makes it not just an interactive movie, the storytelling is different for everyone because of the emergent gameplay feeding into the narrative. There’s a bit where you steal an old woman’s mobility scooter because your neighbour’s convinced she’s faking it. You can refuse, you can question it but if you go there and do it, she’ll chase you then fall and do her hip in. So if you help her and apologise you’ll feel like a bad person and so forth. If you don’t help her though and wait around, she screams and writhes for a bit then gives it up and tells you to f**k off before walking away perfectly normally. Proving your neighbour was right. Just the way you handle every single moment impacts what you’ll get out of it narratively. That’s what makes it a proper game. In many ways, it’s as much a successor to Shenmue as the PS2 GTA games. I cannot stress enough how you need to play it to pass judgment, your own experience with the game will be yours alone.

I just want to make things clear and put things in context for people who haven’t played it yet, who might be confused and want to know what most of the negative ratings is really about, and whether critics have “duped” us with giving the game an undeservedly high score.

First of all, i’d just recommend for people to just play the game for themselves. Or even watch some gameplay online to see what the fuss is about.

First main gripe is people complaining about 30fps.. Well, critics never hid the 30fps things. So that obviously shouldn’t come as a surprise. I guess it didn’t bother them enough , or detract from the positive things enough to lower their score. The game is a graphical and technical masterpiece, and 30fps was a deliberate choice to make that possible. If you’re bothered by it, than yes, it is true. Whether that’s worth a 0/10 for a game of this caliber is obviously debatable, but in my opinion it’s not.

The other issue some people are having is that the game/story is “too woke”. And some of the main reasons for it that i’ve been reading has much to do with the beginning sections where you have to do some chores before the mother of your child gets released from prison.

The house is in a dilapitated state, where the roof is leaking, stairs are broken and a room is half done with drywall everywhere. So to progress in the story you need to fix these things. It literally takes less than 10 mins, if you know where all the fixes are. The other thing is you have to buy some groceries, because there’s nothing in the house and move around some furniture to make the living room look more presentable. And you can buy flowers, but that’s only an optional objective.

So if those things bother you, feel free to stay away from the game. Of course people are allowed to have their opinion. But i think its fair to put some things in perspective and realize that a lot of the reviews 0’s are accompanied by idealogical hyperbole like “feminist slop” and “cuck propaganda”, which doesnt really sound as genuine good faith reviews at all, if thats the only thing your review consists of.

Oh and, when i got the trophy for completing chapter 2, it said that less than 5% of people had earned the trophy. So that says a lot of people haven’t even reached those storylines yet, and i’m assuming a lot of people that scored the game a 0, have not progressed past the few opening hours.

My personal assessment: I will agree that the opening hours had a bit of a slow pacing, but it wasnt that much of an issue to me. Funnily enough the pacing issues i haf had less to do with the chores, but with a small section where Jason boots ip his Playstation and you’re forced to play 3 games for a certain period of time, and its nonskippable. Or where you’re forced to dance in parties. Things like that came across as padding to me, but overall not that big of a deal, and just part of slow world building which is understandable for a game of this scale.

And the hours following the slower intro, even still in chapter 1, already had some of the most memorable moments in gaming, to me. No, I dont see the game as “woke”. And i dont mind the 30fps. So that’s just my 2 cents.

Again, just here to give a bit of clarification for the people that havent played anything but are confused on why its getting review bombed.

I think that the reason GTA is getting review bombed stems from the fact that a lot of reviews don’t actually read like 10/10 reviews from the snippets that are posted on sites like Metacritic. There’s a lot of them that read like they should be lower scored reviews when there’s an isolated sentence or two in them.

I’ll admit that, after 3 hours of gameplay, I’ve thought the game was incredibly impressive, but also it hasn’t felt like the greatest game of all time yet. The intro isn’t as memorable as GTA5’s intro or RDR2’s intro. However, I fully expect that, with the game being bigger and longer, there will be those moments down the line.

Combine that with the entitlement of some gamers over 60 fps, which we all knew was the case prior to release, and we get a segment of the population that can’t believe GTA6 is worth it.

I think part of the bias too is that the game isn’t on PC, so the gamers that sold their consoles to join the PC master race may be feeling left out.

But, as someone that found Baldur’s Gate 3 to be an unplayable buggy mess at launch, I do sympathize some with this consensus. I wouldn’t have given BG3 a zero ever because it’s so obvious that it has greatness all over it and my experience was the anomaly, but still, there may be some out there that are experiencing bugs more frequently than others too and some people just can’t deal with that in games. I mean, some people couldn’t overlook it playing Skyrim years ago. Some people, if they experienced Horizon Forbidden West like I did, might’ve given the game a zero for the hard crashes and lag I had sometimes where I gave it an 8 and mostly ignored those things happened.

Realistically, we’re in a world of extremes with everything nowadays and it’s symptomatic of our culture that trust is gone. It’s a shame, but it’s where we are. We don’t get anywhere condemning people that are overreacting, but from analyzing why, validating their experience exists for a reason, and seeing how that can improve with inclusion. There’s a lot of people that feel excluded in the world now and hate tends to come from a source that causes pain, even if it is misinformed, rather than from simple ignorance.

(Oram77 - just to cover a couple of your specific points: I have no clue what your TV is displaying, except that the framerate of this game does not go above 30. I am also not disagreeing that, on Pro at least (because on base PS5 it is a very different story), it is good enough to be considered locked 30fps with excellent frame pacing.)

R* had the time, budget, and most believe (I'm not convinced either way) ability to do something really special here. They could have kept to this gens standard of 60fps, factoring in any hardware limitations / available CPU budgets, and cleverly used much lower power consuming techniques, but made it look like there was far more going on than there actually was. They would probably have to have left ideas on the table, as the phrase goes, until PS6, or maybe (I don't know) even used them in a 30fps mode only - we have similarly seen plenty of games use RT only in 30fps modes.

Most of game design is a game of smoke and mirrors anyway. We have had things like day/night cycles and changing weather for many (many) years now, its just how accurate the approximation is or how believable the fakery is within the budgets available.

Instead they chose to go back to a last gen standard (30fps), or perhaps more accurately released a cross gen title very early - only time will tell.I wonder how many now will use the excuse of "well, 30fps was good enough for GTA6" or some such like, to justify poor work / insufficient time.

Rating a game as 0/10 is something I would only do if I could get zero enjoyment out of it - in this case, that is perfectly true.

@Nei The issue with trying to objectively evaluate quality is deciding what dictates quality is ultimately subjective. Is a game good because of technical scope? Is it good because of consistent pacing? Good because of story? Good because of entertainment value? Good because of execution? A game can be good for any number of reasons. But what earns it the quality of good is entirely up to the beholder.

The best comparison I can think of is pitting the Mona Lisa against...basically any modern concept art. Is concept art generally more technically accomplished than the Mona Lisa? I'd say so. Does that mean it's better? Does concept art inspire the same emotions and awe as ML? Probably depends on who's looking and what impresses them. As though quality is subjective. And that's not even getting into an appreciation for what was possible during their respective time periods and if that's relevant to their quality — another element to this GTAVI vs. Ocarina discussion.

@RoomWithaMoose See, I completely agree, but then many sports fans (I'm not typically one), here in the UK adore the fact the Sky (Comcast owned) company here broadcasts in 50FPS (yes, you read that right) instead of 30FPS.

So, one could say that action or sports films at the very least could greatly benefit from the additional frames being shown. Then of course, that wouldn't account for a games physical input delay being tied to the visuals, but action in film certainly benefits from more frames.

In fact, a martial arts, or car action scene and even explosions themselves all could be subjectively better to someone the more frames of them they see, smoothing out the motion.

However, though I stated my comment completely in jest, I will cocede that when inputing a response and seeing a response, a smoother set of frames and more of them in the same time period is greatly beneficial.

Having said that though, people tend to forget 24 frames per second for film wasn't done for the ability of it to look smooth like butter.

It was done out of a timing sync issue with audio, whereby they needed to save money on film, yet also have a high enough frame rate to denote "smooth" images creating movement.

So we quite literally as a world more or less, agreed on 24 frames a second despite all knowing it's terrible and in no way beneficial for much of the content Hollywood then began producing.

It is like Rich's point regarding 60 FPS in games being needed for him in many ways, much of the issue he has with 30 FPS games, many indeed do and have had with film and motion in a cinema or at home.

This whole subject raises some important questions really. Especially when yes a game should be aiming for 60FPS, yet a film shooting high involvement of motion should likely aim for higher too.

But then of course the actors wouldn't get as big of a cut of the 200 million budget, if shot on film, as it would cost more, or on SSD RED storage, again, would cost more to store and edit.

People really need to remember though, we don't have 24FPS films because it's a format people actually like, it's the bare minimum film producers could get away with at the time (1920's and onwards), cost, audio and illusion of motion wise.

So it sort of is in many ways much like how GTA 6 is 30FPS, they recognise it's a bare minimum and it's fair to say aimed for it, knowing for well they will indeed achieve 60FPS on the PS6.

Much like how we could now achieve 60FPS in film, but that would require an entire world protest and uproar, and seeing as many people don't even visit the cinema or buy films any more, it's sort of a moot point.

But yes, totally get your point and don't discount it or disagree.

#3950. In a reveal that might worry eventual PC players glancing at their GPUs, GTA 6 will target 30fps on all consoles

Oh, and and it'll be streamable on the Xbox One before it's playable on PC

In a press release coinciding with Grand Theft Auto VI becoming available for pre-load ahead of its November 19th release date, Rockstar has confirmed that the game "has been fully developed from the ground up to provide the best possible experience for the current generation of consoles, targeting 30 frames per second while pushing both platforms to their absolute limits." Read between the lines, and you can kind of make out the words "...so hope your PCs are up to spec, computer nerds."

GTA 6, of course, still does not have a confirmed PC version, even if Rockstar's former tech director says it's probably not far off. And despite this, even ancient, last-gen consoles are getting in on it, as the release also unexpectedly confirms that the game will be playable on Xbox One via Xbox Cloud Gaming, Microsoft's game streaming service that has suddenly lost its ability to work on PC. Granted, this comes with a warning: "as with all cloud streaming, connection speeds and other technical factors may influence game performance in ways that would not impact local gameplay." If you ended up getting a PS4 last generation, no cloud play for you either, I'm afraid. It also states that it will "play best on Playstation 5 consoles", making great use of that Sony partnership, and will include Playstation Spectral Super Resolution and ray-traced shadows on PS5 Pro.

A 2026 current-gen game targeting 30fps, let alone one as titanic of a release as GTA VI, is probably not going to go down well with a lot of people, even if console players are traditionally les sensitive about FPS counts than PC players. What this does imply, though, is that the inevitable PC release might be an even more demanding behemoth than expected, if Xbox Series and PS5 versions can't even target 60fps. The availability of the game on Xbox One, even if just through cloud streaming, could have resulted in an acceptance that 60fps just wasn't going to be possible if it was also going to be able to 'run' on last-gen hardware. Either way, when it does eventually escape console exclusivity, hopefully trying to run GTA VI on anything less than an RTX 5080 won't set your PC on fire. Now, let me just quickly have a glance at GPU prices. Oh, no.

#3949. Bandai Namco is liquidating Unknown 9: Awakening studio Reflector Entertainment, following multiple previous layoffs since the game's launch

As another addition to the slew of smaller studios being dissolved by their parent companies, Bandai Namco announced in a press release that they are shutting down their subsidiary studio Reflector Entertainment, a Montreal studio responsible for 2024's action-adventure game Unknown 9: Awakening. In its notice, Bandai Namco explains that the reason for the liquidation is due to Reflector not meeting its expectations for "future business plans, necessary additional investment, and the possibility of profitability and business continuation."

The press release notes that the liquidation of Reflector will result in an estimated "extraordinary loss" of around 21 million euros, or 3.5 billion yen, for Bandai Namco in its Q3 fiscal report of this year. This is not the first time Reflector has been cut by Bandai, as around a month after the launch of Unknown 9: Awakening and presumably in response to its low sales, 18% of the workforce was laid off. 2025 then saw further redundancies amidst the cancellation of a prospective project, though details on those layoffs were not granted by the company. Unknown 9 was intended to be a transmedia franchise involving the game as well as comic books and novels, but these ambitions never came to pass.

Bandai Namco notes that the liquidation will be held to local laws and procedures, which make the actual schedule of the process uncertain for now. A similar process faces Arkane Lyon, which is currently in a purgatory of having been chosen for closure by Microsoft, but temporarily protected by French labor laws that prevent it from being suddenly closed without proper negotiation and procedure.

#3946. Company of Heroes 3 developer admits "it was a lot" to make the 3.0 overhaul patch alongside regular updates, singleplayer DLC, and a whole spinoff game

The Company of Heroes 3's 3.0 update is huge. Touching virtually every part of the three-year-old RTS, the patch notes are longer than, well, my arm isn't a great measure of patch note length. Let's just say the headline features of overhauled VFX and audio don't really cover it. It also comes with new autumn and winter biomes, an updated grand strategy campaign, improvements to unit AI, and a whole host of other changes.

Talking to Relic ahead of the 3.0 update's launch I learned a little more about the scale of work that went on behind the scenes to make it happen, but also a little more about why Relic are still supporting the game three years after it was released and two years after separating from Sega.

The team began planning the 3.0 update two years ago, seeing the series' 20th anniversary as an opportunity to make a significant update to Company of Heroes 3, and focus on issues players had flagged since launch. "The VFX were called out," executive producer Denise Christie tells me. "Same thing with a lot of our audio."

Relic were already releasing patches every three months, but the changes they were looking at were much too large for those smaller updates. If they had tried to do the work as part of the small updates, approaching the problems with piecemeal solutions, it would have turned Company of Heroes 3 into a hodgepodge of new and old assets. "We wanted to make sure it was a cohesive package," principal designer Eric Wrobel says. "If you increase the quality of one thing, you have to do it equally across so much stuff." Otherwise you end up with "One that looks awesome and one that's like, 'Oh, this one's kind of gross'."

Complicating matters, though, was that the team couldn't down tools and focus on just these large changes. As well as the small patches that were still going out every three months, both the VFX and audio teams were also contributing the battlegroup DLC packs which added new units to the game. "They would work on stuff and in one branch that was the 3.0 work and then they would go ahead and do some battlegroup stuff and come back to that," Christie says. "It was a lot."

As the 3.0 update grew in scope, it also meant other departments were contributing to the anniversary release while working on the smaller updates and DLC. "For us to create future maps for Company of Heroes 3, we were going to have an issue that our assets were getting stale," Christie explains. So, as part of 3.0, Relic's art department created autumn and winter asset packs, as well as a new Industrial theme. This then created more work for the VFX team, who have added rain and snow, as well as a transition effect showing soil and concrete moving from dry to wet.

Not to be outdone, the design team also made significant changes to the singleplayer Italy campaign. The towns that dot the dynamic grand strategy-inspired map now have individual upgrades, making for more meaningful decisions when it comes to which settlement you capture next. And, responding to one of the main criticisms of Company of Heroes 3's singleplayer, they also updated the computer's AI so it makes smarter decisions in both the turn-based and real-time battles. "We wanted to get this feel like there was that sort of back and forth of the AI resisting you and pushing forward into your territory and actually taking your stuff, which wasn't really happening in any of the previous updates," Wrobel says.

Further complicating matters was the fact that alongside these regular updates, the DLC, and the big 3.0 update release work, was that Relic also released Final Stand in July, a roguelike horde mode spinoff of Company of Heroes 3. "We had to be very careful not to accidentally introduce this 3.0 work that was also happening at the same time," Christie says." The improvements in this update have also rolled out for the spinoff, too.

Naturally, Relic aren't doing all this work purely out of the goodness of the hearts. The regular updates keep players engaged, Christie explains, and "hopefully bring back lapsed players who were frustrated by some of these things." It's something the team have already seen happen before, Wrobel explains. "We saw with the 2.0 update that we had a big spike of users and that was great, but because that improved the overall quality of the game, we saw each month we were selling more copies than we were before. People have been buying these games for years and years and years, so if we invest in this now we're going to see returns for quite a long time into the future as well."

"If we were starting to see that tail down then we probably would have made a very different decision to be honest, but that's not what we see," Christie adds.

The next release for Company of Heroes 3 is a singleplayer DLC, Operation Torch, due out on November 25th. (So, if you're keeping count, that was also in the works while the update, battlegroup DLC, and spinoff were all being made.) Until now, Relic's additions to the RTS have been focused on the multiplayer community, adding new units to be used online or in offline skirmishes. Operation Torch brings new scripted missions that trace a set of soldiers moving through North Africa.

After that, though, I ask if Relic plans to continue adding to Company of Heroes 3 or if they're ready to move onto a new project. "Well, it's both actually," CEO Justin Dowdeswell tells me. "We would love to continue with Company of Heroes 3 and not solely as a place for us to experiment. That's one of the advantages of being smaller, and being able to make decisions. We're not going to leave Company of Heroes 3. It's an and function. We are going to embark on the next thing."

So, it doesn't sound like Relic are taking anything off their plate…

Kodak Black and The Vault nightclub each have their own unique playlist.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Rockstar's lengthy credits reveal just how massive the GTA 6 song list truly is, but you don't start the game with every radio station unlocked. Leonida has two secret playlists (both needed for 100% completion), and neither is particularly hard to unlock once you know where to look.

The Sniper of La Perle, Kodak Black's 22-track playlist, becomes available as soon as you scan four posters around La Perle at TWA Ponya Tattoo, Drip Drops, Aunt Zola's Soul Food, and the Jack of Hearts nightclub. Then there's The Vault Radio, which only requires you to scan a single poster at the nightclub of the same name.

The shops automatically marked themselves on my map as I drove around La Perle and Crosstown, but I've included screenshots highlighting their specific locations in Vice City's Haitian district. Once you arrive at one, Jason or Lucia's phone should alert you to something nearby you can scan with a notification from the Waink It app.

Look right as soon as you enter the parlor. There's a Sniper of Perle poster on the small table by the door.

You'll find another Sniper of Perle poster lying on the cash register counter.

The Sniper of Perle poster is immediately to the left as you enter, on a corkboard in front of the cash register.

Head upstairs to the second floor and enter the Jack of Hearts recording studio. Pass through the lobby and into the control room, then you'll see the Sniper of Perle poster lying on the table beside a fan.

Once you arrive at the nightclub, head through the entrance corridor and look at the back wall. The poster is right there, and one quick scan is all it takes to unlock The Vault's playlist.

#3942. Nvidia shareholders have filed a lawsuit against the tech company over claims that they were misled regarding CEO Jensen Huang's affair

If I wasn't so sick of hearing about AI every day of my life at the moment I might have found it funny to hear that one of the biggest peddlers of the poison around Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was caught having an affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Oh who am I kidding, it is funny! And despite knowing that this won't likely push Nvidia away from AI, I am a bit tickled to hear that the tech company and Huang are on the receiving end of a lawsuit.

The suit in question, as reported by The Guardian, is based on a complaint filed in California's federal court on behalf of Mark Kistenmacher by Rosen Law Firm. Kistenmacher is an Nvidia shareholder, and with this suit he's seeking to "recover compensable damages," for himself and other shareholders due to the "precipitous decline in the market value of the Company’s securities." What a palaver! I do not imagine this will be resolved particularly quickly.

As it currently stands, Huang has only admitted to having an affair rather than any trade secrets being leaked anywhere. Nvidia had this to say on the matter: "While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information. Jensen fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it. The Board has confidence in Jensen and his leadership team and will provide further updates as appropriate."

The concern comes from the person Huang had an affair with, one Alice Huang (no, they aren't related), a former managing director of Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data centre company who have allegedly given Chinese companies Nvidia chips they bought billions of US dollars of. A messy situation to be sure, and one I unconfidently hope brings about the end of AI, somehow.

#3941. Marathon is becoming a whole new game next month with a roguelite PvE mode, a beta for a very Halo-esque team deathmatch mode, a vibey social space and more

Marathon is getting a lot bigger next month. In September, Bungie outlined their plans for the shooter making some big promises, namely the arrival of a PvE mode, and now they've shown off what you can expect from its next season, Symbiosis.

Top of the order is that PvE mode, which has a name now: Expedition. It's a roguelite mode, one that's playable in co-op, though a lack of details at this current time doesn't make it clear as to whether you can run it solo or not. The season's trailer, which you can have a gander at below, gives off the impression that you'll have to complete particular tasks before exfiltrating like you normally do. I'm sure we'll learn more in time.

The previously promised social space will be coming with this update too, and it's called Limbo. Morbidly appropriate! You can hang out here with your buds, head to a mini arena for some impromptu matches (I think), or head to the firing range where you can test out your weapons. You'll also be able to try out the new runner shell, Bishop, a cooler than you, samurai-sword-wielding robot who can jump real good and do that cool movie thing where it slices a whole bunch of enemies at once in one swing real quick like.

What will undoubtedly have some folks going "Halo's back!" is the beginning of a beta test for a team deathmatch mode. The Halo comparison is apt not simply because of the fact that it's Bungie who are making it, but because there's a deep-voiced announcer guy talking about all the sick kills you do. Details are slim on how this will work too. Beyond that, there's a few new weapons to flaunt, and maybe most excitingly, big ole alien enemies to take on.

You've still got a little while to wait for Symbiosis, which is currently slated to launch on December 8th. The game will be free to play from then until December 15th, too, obviously in a bid to show sceptics how good it is now (hopefully it is good, for Bungie's sake).

#3940. Zenless Zone Zero version 3.4 update ‘The Finality of the Day’ launches December 2

The version 3.4 update for Zenless Zone Zero, dubbed “The Finality of the Day,” will launch on December 2, developer miHoYo announced.

Here is an overview of the update, via miHoYo:

The story of the Sky Island of Roscaelifer reaches its final climax, as Sunbringer, a new Void Hunter and the first Enchainer Agent, joins the fight. The new version also kicks off the Zenless Zone Zero × Honkai: Star Rail collaboration, introducing two crossover Agents, Robin and Kafka, along with themed events. It also brings new combat gameplay, updates to permanent game modes, and a variety of version rewards.

In Version 3.4, Roscaelifer’s main story is about to reach its climax. From the Bangboo corruption incident to High Ambitions Corp.’s invasion, the Proxies and their allies have weathered crisis after crisis together. Now, the enemy has stepped out of the shadows, and Roscaelifer faces a decisive battle for its very survival. For the first time, the three Sunbringers — Dracaene, Lindverne, and Eldreda—will fight side-by-side, joining the Proxies to take on a formidable foe and defend Roscaelifer. New characters and menacing enemies are taking the stage, while the arrival of an unexpected character leaves even more mysteries hanging over this new chapter. How will this storm change the fate of the Celestial Nexus? What trials await the Proxies and their allies? All will be revealed in “The Finality of the Day.”

Once this version update goes live, Sunbringer, leader of Roscaelifer, joins the fray as an S-Rank Genesis Flare Armorer Agent, bringing a unique offensive and defensive rhythm through a three-member synergistic combat style: Eldreda, Lindverne, and Dracaene take turns stepping in with a lance, greatsword, and shield, seamlessly balancing offense and defense. Their Armorer attacks can stack Gash on enemies, and consuming Gash triggers Maim while building up Wishfire. Once Wishfire is sufficient, Eldreda can hold Basic Attack to hurl her lance and make her entrance, following up with a synergy Chain Attack. When Decibels are sufficient, they can unleash a two-stage Ultimate that detonates all Embermark stacks on the enemy at once, triggering Emberburst for massive damage. When the new version launches, Proxies can obtain Sunbringer and the S-Rank Armorer W-Engine Dragonfire Mirage via Signal Search. On top of that, the new Bangboo Sleepwalkerboo will also arrive in the Bangboo Channel, summoning Bangboo soldiers to back you up in combat and boosting Sunbringer’s damage when Sunbringer is on the squad.

The two crossover Agents also bring their own distinct combat styles. Robin can keep up her Concerto performance off-field, granting teammates shields while boosting their DEF and DMG, and can extend her support effects by re-entering the field. Her Ultimate can also restore Sharpness for Armorer Agents. Meanwhile, Kafka, an S-Rank Electric Agent, builds her offense around Attribute Anomalies and Disorder DMG. While in the Hunter’s Overture state, she can choose between slashing or shooting attacks, enhancing direct DMG or speeding up Attribute Anomaly buildup, respectively. When her slashes hit an enemy afflicted with an Attribute Anomaly, she can also trigger a Lightning Surge to deal additional DMG. Robin’s brand-new outfit, Cosmic Beat, will also be made available. Sunbringer’s and Robin’s Signal Search channels will open on the first day of the update and run throughout Version 3.4, while Kafka will arrive in the second half of the version. As for reruns, the S-Rank Physical Anomaly Agent Alice and the S-Rank Anomaly W-Engine Practiced Perfection will return in the second half of the version.

Beyond combat, Dracaene, Lindverne, and Eldreda will each have their own Trust Events, showcasing the distinct daily lives of the three Sunbringers. Once all three reach max trust level, Proxies will also unlock a special side quest to help secretly plan their birthday party. Their new daily wear outfit, Moonlit Promenade, reveals a side of the three Sunbringers as they step into city life, letting Proxies experience up close Dracaene’s gentle sweetness, Lindverne’s playful personality, and Eldreda’s bold, free-spirited charm. The Moonlit Promenade outfit set and its matching Starlit Stroll Limited Gift will also be available. The latter includes a three-person Accompany Experience and an exclusive Idle Action, so Proxies can enjoy their everyday company on the streets of New Eridu. A dynamic wallpaper and three matching Inter-Knot avatars will also arrive with this version.

As for events, the collab event “Lost in a Theatrical Dream” between Zenless Zone Zero and Honkai: Star Rail kicks off in Version 3.4. Proxies will team up with Robin, Kafka, and their New Eridu companions to film a series, featuring stealth raids and Agent interactions. Complete the event to score rewards like the collab Bangboo Pom-Pom and Polychromes. On top of that, the new version also brings the “Opening Act: Enter the Knight” combat mode and a new “Dark Dungeon Survival” season for Enigma of the Labyrinth. Proxies can join in to earn Polychromes, a profile icon, new accessories, and more.

As for rewards, after the Version 3.4 update, log in to claim the limited collab S-Rank Agent Robin for free, along with the upgrade materials needed to raise her to Lv. 40 and a full set of Drive Discs with matching Main Stats. During the version, Proxies will also receive overclock materials for the W-Engine Twilight Afterimage and all remaining Agent Focus: Pyrois for free, and check-in and web events will be available. To thank Proxies around the world for sticking with us, starting January 1, Proxies can claim up to 1,600 Polychromes in total through daily login check-ins. During the version, Zenless Zone Zero will also partner with Make-A-Wish on a charitable initiative, inviting the community to join Sunbringer in helping support wishes for children with critical illnesses. The “Filmgoer Thank-You Gift” cumulative top-up event will also run during the version. Proxies can earn commemorative ticket stubs by purchasing Monochromes or the New Eridu City Fund, Inter-Knot Membership, or cash bundles. Collect enough ticket stubs to unlock rewards such as an S-Rank Agent and W-Engine of your choice. Kafka’s signature W-Engine Requiem Araneae will also be available in the W-Engine selection pool. The event also offers personalized rewards, including a Sunbringer-themed animated namecard, a sidebar theme and pendant, and collab-themed accessories.

Zenless Zone Zero is available now for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series, PC via client download, Steam, and Epic Games Store, iOS via App Store, and Android via Google Play.

Simping aside, Vicki may actually sound familiar because her voice actor is Taryn Manning, who had a pretty major role as Tiffany ‘Pennsatucky’ Doggett in Orange Is the New Black.

The 48-year-old actress has also starred in a variety of other shows like Sons of Anarchy, and has even had parts in movies like Hustle & Flow and the 8-Mile.

There are a lot of characters to keep track of in GTA 6, but Vicki is definitely one that stuck with me, largely because she’s pivotal to one of my favourite missions in the game.

#3938. Robert Downey Jr., Chris Evans, the Russo brothers, and more on the making of Avengers: Infinity War

Join the GamesRadar community for quick access. Enter your email below and we'll send confirmation, and sign you up to our newsletter.
